This is a major deal for anyone thinking about renouncing US citizenship.

According to recent reports, many assume they can keep visiting the US after renunciation on ESTA based on their other citizenship. But there are more and more reports of former citizens being denied ESTA and told to apply for a visitor visa instead.

According to recent reports, A visitor visa, unlike ESTA, generally requires a consular interview and proving that the applicant will leave after the visit. With family, businesses, or assets in the US, that could mean delays and refusals. This has to factor into the decision on whether or not to renounce.

    Industry News: Even Putin Is a ’90s Nostalgist

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (207 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Nationalreview

    ⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that in Abu Dhabi for peace talks, Russian negotiators revealed that Vladimir Putin is just like the rest of us, a nostalgist for the 1990s.
    • The Russian demand is chiefly about geography.
    • Michael Brendan Dougherty is a senior writer at National Review Online.

    Recent findings suggest that in Abu Dhabi for peace talks, Russian negotiators revealed that Vladimir Putin is just like the rest of us, a nostalgist for the 1990s. You and I might want to go back for the easeful sense of prosperity, the pre-9/11 sense of security, the pre-Instagram sense of contentment for the pleasures of your own life, or the still-unified popular culture that gave an entire diverse country something in common to talk about at work. Vladimir Putin’s men reiterated one of their primary pre-Ukraine war demands: Russia wants NATO to be back in its 1997 positions.

    Well, sort of. The Russian demand is chiefly about geography. If it were done, it would mean removing nine battlegroups in total: Sweden, in Finland; the U.K., in Estonia; Canada, in Latvia; Germany, in Lithuania; France, in Romania; Spain, in Slovakia; Italy, in Bulgaria; and the U.S., which has 10,000 men in Poland now but only 300 of them permanently there. The U.S. has Aegis Ashore weapons sites in Romania and Northern Poland, and there is a multinational, NATO division-level command center headquartered in northeastern Poland.

    Michael Brendan Dougherty is a senior writer at National Review Online.

    On “Even Putin Is a ’90s Nostalgist”.

    Recent findings suggest that southwest Airlines will give you a Companion Pass for a single holiday roundtrip, even if you book the cheapest Basic fare with points. From January 8 through March 3, 2027, you can bring someone on as many trips as you like for just the taxes and fees (from $5.60 each way). You can use points for your seat then, too.

    It has been revealed that register for the Black Friday offer first, then book by 11:59 p.m. Central on Sunday, November 29. Put your Rapid Rewards number on the reservation when you book.

    Already booked for Christmas? If the same award or paid ticket still costs the same, then register, cancel and rebook. And for a winter trip where you’ll use the pass, you can book your seat now and add your companion once the pass is active, as long as there’s still a seat for sale.

    Recent findings suggest that southwest gets your Christmas booking this weekend and gives you the second seat after the holiday rush. If you earned the pass they offered in August, yours starts January 5 and also ends March 3. This offer adds zero days. You get one designated companion at a time across all your passes, with three changes for 2027 after you pick the first person.

    I used to buy my ticket, bring my wife as my companion and redeem points for our daughter. With two kids, I’d register both parents. Each can earn a pass and designate a child. If one parent already earned August’s pass, only the other needs to qualify this time. Fly Austin to Orlando and back nonstop in February and the two kids’ tickets together would cost $22.40 in taxes and fees, even if both parents use points.

    This year it takes 135,000 Companion Pass qualifying points or 100 qualifying one-way flights to earn the full pass. Under the Rapid Rewards changes for 2027, unlimited companion travel comes with Platinum status starting January 1. That takes the same 100 flights – or 140,000 tier qualifying points. At 75 flights or 95,000 tier qualifying points you get three companion trips, each of which can be a roundtrip. What made the old pass so easy to earn was that a credit card initial bonus could cover most of those 135,000 points. Next year initial bonuses, referral and anniversary points, extra points from card bonus categories, and points from hotel and rental car partners stop counting toward the pass. A Southwest credit card earns one tier qualifying point per dollar, and cardmembers get a 10,000 point boost when they reach 130,000. Earning the full pass on card spend alone takes $130,000 in purchases. Southwest has also extended the credit card application deadline from December 2 to December 14. Apply by then and get approved, and the 80,000 or 90,000 point initial bonus can count toward the old 135,000 point requirement for a companion pass earned in 2026 even if you finish the required spending in early 2027. Southwest Rapid Rewards® Plus Credit Card (See rates and fees) earn 80,000 bonus points after spending $1,000 on purchases in the first 3 months from account opening. Southwest Rapid Rewards® Priority Credit Card (See rates and fees) earn 90,000 bonus points after spending $3,000 on purchases in the first 3 months from account opening. Any ordinary purchase points you need to close the gap still have to post in 2026. The pass you earn this way runs through December 31, 2027.     #157176. Breaking: Departing Senate spending kingpins angle for last earmark hurrah

    Breaking: Departing Senate spending kingpins angle for last earmark hurrah

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (828 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Susan Collins, R-Maine, left, and Mitch McConnell , R-Ky., won't be smiling as much if Democrats force a punt on spending bills to next year.
    • Newly released Senate appropriations bills would distribute $8.7 billion in "congressionally directed spending" secured by 78 senators for their home states — earmarked dollars that could disappear if Congress resorts to a stopgap funding measure to avert a partial government shutdown after Dec.
    • Nearly 4,000 individual earmarks are contained in nine of the 12 draft fiscal 2027 spending bills, a CQ Roll Call tally found; the remaining three bills — Defense, State-Foreign Operations and Legislative Branch — don't have any.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that sens. Susan Collins, R-Maine, left, and Mitch McConnell , R-Ky., won't be smiling as much if Democrats force a punt on spending bills to next year. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call file photo).

    Newly released Senate appropriations bills would distribute $8.7 billion in "congressionally directed spending" secured by 78 senators for their home states — earmarked dollars that could disappear if Congress resorts to a stopgap funding measure to avert a partial government shutdown after Dec. 11.

    Nearly 4,000 individual earmarks are contained in nine of the 12 draft fiscal 2027 spending bills, a CQ Roll Call tally found; the remaining three bills — Defense, State-Foreign Operations and Legislative Branch — don't have any.

    It has been revealed that there's typically some overlap between House and Senate projects that would get weeded out in final negotiations to avoid duplication. But for comparison's sake, House Republicans included nearly 6,700 line items worth $8.2 billion in their earmarked spending bills.

    Democrats have signaled they'll push for a continuing resolution into the first quarter of next year enabling them to rewrite the full-year fiscal 2027 bills when they take the gavels in January, possibly upping the overall pot of earmarked funds — or at least divvying up the pie more favorably to blue states and districts.

    But that would mean the final attempt by departing lawmakers like Senate Appropriations Chair Susan Collins, R-Maine, and longtime Senate GOP leader and senior appropriator Mitch McConnell of Kentucky, to deliver for their states might be all for naught.

    And top Democrats with substantial earmarking success under GOP governance, such as Appropriations ranking member Patty Murray, D-Wash., will have to start from scratch.

    Here are some key stats on senators' earmarks in the latest batch of spending bills Collins is trying to get across the finish line.

    Naturally, much of the spoils go to Senate Appropriations Committee members, and that's no different this year. But with so many more Democrats requesting projects — often jointly with their fellow delegation member — individual contributions may appear diluted given they have to share the credit.

    Industry observers note that that dilution shows up in the rankings when allocating credit in a way that avoids double-counting — everyone gets an equal share of his or her joint projects, so $20 million sponsored jointly by two senators will appear as $10 million for each. Solo earmarkers in this scenario face no such dilution.

    Using the even-split methodology, the top 10 — all senior appropriators — look like this:.

    Another way to look at it is by simply adding up every instance of a senator affixing his or her name to a project, which leads to double-counting but gives them full credit for every earmark secured, even with jointly requested projects.

    Here's the top 10 in that scenario:.

    Finally, there's the solo earmarker leaderboard, only counting dollars secured without any co-sponsors:.

    McConnell and Collins hit the trifecta, ending up among the top three in all three scenarios.

    Related: Maine senators at odds over credit for earmarks.

    Unlike the House, where states with the largest populations receive the most funding by virtue of having more representatives securing earmarks, smaller states punch above their weight in the Senate — particularly when their delegations achieve exalted positions of seniority.

    Hence Washington state — with Murray and Cantwell, the Commerce Committee ranking member, representing it — is way out in front.

    Sources indicate that by contrast, the second- and third-most populous states — Texas and Florida — received a grand total of zero earmarked funds, because their GOP senators didn't request any. California, with the largest population, is No. 16 in the ranks; New York is 12th.

    Here are the top 10 states by earmarked funds procured in the Senate bills, clearly skewing toward smaller, typically reddish states:.

    In a recent development, the Transportation-HUD spending bill continues to be the go-to place for earmarks, accounting for 27 percent of all individual projects in the Senate bills and about one-third of all the earmarked dollars. The next-closest bill, Labor-HHS-Education, has half the earmarked amount that the "T-HUD" bill does.

    Top agencies and programs with earmarked funds are housed within, that's right, the departments of Transportation and Housing and Urban Development, with HUD leading the pack thanks to its ever-popular Community Development Fund accounting for all of that department's earmarks.

    Transportation isn't far behind, thanks largely to highway projects, followed by Health and Human Services and its Health Resources and Services Administration account, which funds community health centers. Defense Department military construction projects and the Army Corps of Engineers round out the group of $1 billion-plus agencies.

    Here are the top accounts for earmarked funds in this year's crop of bills:.

    The biggest individual earmarks are largely within Army Corps accounts funded in the draft Energy-Water bill, with some military construction and transportation projects and two mega NIST-based university construction earmarks thrown in on behalf of Collins and McConnell.

    Ashley Schapitl complains that a New York Hampton Inn can run $700 to $800 a night. She’s elected neighborhood commissioner in Washington, D.C. and works for a lobby shop. She was deputy assistant secretary for public affairs at Treasury during the Biden administration. What she seems not to realize is that the cost of New York City hotel rooms was a political choice engineered to protect incumbents from competition, drive up rates, and make it possible to redistribute excess profits to hotel unions. NYC hotel prices are out of control. There is no world in which the Hampton Inn should cost $700-$800 a night.— Ashley Schapitl (@AshleySchapitl) November 24, 2026 One reply suggested HotelTonight, another told her to get her money up, but the correct take was the one who mentioned to “Thank Neal Kwatra” the former political director of New York’s hotel workers union. New York would be expensive anyway. Land and construction are costly (the latter is not unrelated) and there remains strong demand. But higher costs were intentional policy. The City Limited New Hotels In December 2021, New York extended its hotel permit requirement citywide. Even on land already zoned for hotels, most projects need the City Planning Commission’s approval, subject to City Council review. This was a pet policy initiative of the Hotel and Gaming Trades Council. Even projects expected to pass can take two to three years to get a permit No one expects that a nonunion hotel could ever get approved. The union gets an effective veto over new projects. City planners outlined that the new rules could be expected to reduce the number of new rooms in the city by over 25% – down to 127,660 by 2035 versus 174,730 without the policy. They also projected 18,970 fewer hotel jobs. This wasn’t a byproduct of the policy, it was the point – less supply, higher rates, redistribute income to incumbent workers. As I wrote when this was proposed, existing hotel owners and the union both have something to gain. Less competition makes an existing room more profitable. A strike would leave those expensive rooms empty, so the union can bargain for the difference. The Airbnb Crackdown Was Part Of This, Too In 2023 New York began barring Airbnb and other platforms from processing unregistered bookings. For stays under 30 days, the host generally has to stay in the apartment and can take only two paying guests. That limits supply but makes the argument for new hotels even stronger, but those are effectively barred too. A study in the European Journal of Political Economy estimated that the short-term rental crackdown added $14 to $19 to the average hotel night. Hotels took in an estimated $2.1 billion to $2.9 billion more over the first 18 months while selling roughly the same number of nights. Local Businesses Are Hurt, Too A family that cuts a three-night New York trip to two buys one fewer dinner. Another goes somewhere else instead. Or they do the full New York trip but spend less while they’re there. Restaurants see less money. There are fewer restaurant jobs, and tip income for waiters goes down. A working paper tracking card transactions across 19 metro areas estimated that after the Airbnb crackdown, New York restaurant spending fell 7.5%. Restaurants that relied on out-of-town diners took a disproportionate hit. In neighboring New Jersey markets, restaurant spending rose 10.1%. And the hotel effect magnifies this further.     📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Southwest Airlines’ Companion Pass, which allows you to bring a friend nearly for free (you just have to pay the taxes and fees) on unlimited flights, is one of the most valuable assets in the world of points and miles.

    It normally takes a whole lot of flying to unlock this pass — and one of the popular shortcuts that allows you to earn this pass with points from Southwest credit card bonuses is ending soon, which will only make it even harder to earn.

    According to recent reports, but if you'd rather spend your Black Friday weekend booking flights than buying discounted sweatpants, there is some good news. There's a new limited-time opportunity to earn a promotional Southwest Companion Pass if you book one round-trip or two one-way eligible Southwest flights by Sunday, Nov. 29, 2026, and travel on those flights by Jan. 5, 2027.

    Your promotional Companion Pass would then be valid for unlimited use between Jan. 8, 2027, and March 3, 2027.

    In a recent development, first, register for the promotion with your Southwest Rapid Rewards number. Then, book one qualifying round-trip flight or two one-way flights using your Rapid Rewards number by 11:59 p.m. CST on Sunday, Nov. 29. Flights must be completed sometime from Nov. 27 to Jan. 5, 2027.

    Sources indicate that successfully complete the above steps, and you'll earn a promotional Companion Pass valid for use between Jan. 8 and March 3, 2027.

    All fare classes, including the carrier’s Basic option, are eligible for this promotion. And it doesn’t matter how you pay for your flight, as there's no specific spending requirement. Rapid Rewards point redemptions and Cash + Points bookings qualify too, as long as you book through Southwest channels, such as the carrier’s website or mobile app.

    If you have existing flights on Southwest, they won't automatically count for this promotion. However, if you can cancel those reservations, register and rebook before the promotion ends on Sunday, that should work (provided you complete your travel within the qualifying travel window). Be sure to check for any fare differences before canceling.

    In a recent development, southwest’s Companion Pass is almost legendary in the world of points and miles. It lets you bring a companion along on unlimited flights, whether you book with cash or points, for almost free. As long as there’s an open seat on the plane, your companion can fly with you for just the cost of taxes and fees (which start at $5.60).

    Recent findings suggest that you must designate a companion in your Rapid Rewards account. However, you’re allowed to change your designated companion up to three times per year, and this rule applies to promotional passes as well.

    If you'd like to earn a Companion Pass for longer than just eight weeks or so this promotional pass is valid, there is still time to earn a Companion Pass for all of 2027 using the welcome bonuses from the Southwest credit cards as outlined here. You have to act swiftly, though, since those rules are changing soon.

    Related: Best Southwest Airlines credit cards.

    Sources indicate that the Southwest Companion Pass can be extremely valuable for those who like to travel with a companion. Earning one is about to become a lot harder, so this is a great promotion for those who can register, book eligible travel by Sunday and travel between now and Jan. 5, 2027.

    According to recent reports, the Citi® / AAdvantage BusinessTM World Elite Mastercard® [See rates and fees] can turn $125,000 in eligible spending on an employee card into American Airlines Platinum Pro status for two people. That’s without even earning any Loyalty Points from flying, a hotel booking or shopping through American’s portal.

    In a recent development, the Citi AAdvantage Business Card is the best airline credit card for spending toward status. I have the card, and I’m keeping it. The limited-time initial bonus is strong, the first year has no annual fee, and the recently unveiled refresh adds benefits. But the reason to put spending on this card is that two people can get status credit for the same purchases.

    The current limited time offer is 75,000 American Airlines AAdvantage bonus miles after $5,000 in purchases within the first five months of account opening. Purchases by the primary cardmember and employees count toward that requirement. There’s no annual fee for the first 12 months. The card’s regular annual fee is right now $99, but it rises to $150 with renewals beginning January 24, 2027. Someone opening the card now will see a $150 annual fee at renewal. Employee cards have no additional annual fee, and there’s no foreign transaction fee. The initial bonus alone can cover a one way Japan Airlines business class award between the U.S. and Japan when partner award space is available. American miles remain especially strong for premium cabin awards on partners. Prices largely remain at the same level they were a decade ago, while numerous other progams have devalued. Citi’s 48 month restriction applies to an initial bonus on this business card, including its former CitiBusiness AAdvantage Platinum Select-named product. Citi also restricts eligibility after converting another Citi account with a recent initial bonus into this product. Having a separate personal American Airlines card doesn’t, by itself, disqualify you. How The Same Citi AAdvantage Business Card Spending Earns Status For Two People Normally each cardmember earns one Loyalty Point per dollar on their purchases. When an employee uses their card, those Loyalty Points go to the employee. Through December 31, 2028, the primary cardmember also receives one Loyalty Point per dollar of eligible employee card spending. That’s an additional credit to a second person’s account. Spending on the primary cardmember’s card still earns that person one Loyalty Point per dollar. When I covered the refresh, American confirmed to me that all Citi AAdvantage Business cardmembers were included after the former Barclays business accounts migrated. This used to be called a targeted promotion because legacy Barclays cardmembers didn’t qualify. Here’s what eligible spending on one employee’s card can accomplish in a single status qualification year, assuming neither person earns Loyalty Points elsewhere: Employee Card Spending Primary Cardmember Employee $40,000 Gold Gold $75,000 Platinum Platinum $125,000 Platinum Pro Platinum Pro $200,000 Executive Platinum Executive Platinum American’s qualification year starts March 1 and runs through the end of February. You can combine the card’s Loyalty Points with qualifying activity from other sources. A business owner with several employee cards receives the additional Loyalty Points across their eligible spending. Each employee gets credit for the purchases on their individual card. Authorized owners must be employees or contractors of the business, and need to be enrolled in AAdvantage and AAdvantage Business to receive their Loyalty Points. A spouse who works in the business fits this. The Business Controls The Miles Redeemable miles work differently from status credit. The miles from purchases, including employee purchases, and the initial bonus go into the firm’s AAdvantage Business account. The business can then transfer miles to registered travelers’ personal AAdvantage accounts, including the primary cardmember’s. You don’t have to decide which person will ultimately use the miles when you make a purchase. So unlike a consumer card where the miles go into the primary cardmember’s account, these are transferable AAdvantage miles. The Citi® / AAdvantage BusinessTM World Elite Mastercard® also waives American’s small business program’s usual requirements of five active travelers and $5,000 in eligible American Airlines flight spending to access earned miles. That lets you ‘double tip’ with American, earning business program miles and miles from the same travel, and tickets credited to a small business account earn an extra loyalty point per dollar spent too. The AAdvantage Business program awards the company one mile per eligible airfare dollar and registered travelers one additional Loyalty Point per eligible airfare dollar. What You Earn On Purchases The Citi AAdvantage Business Card currently earns: 2 miles per dollar on eligible American Airlines purchases. 2 miles per dollar at gas stations, car rental merchants, telecommunications merchants, and cable and satellite providers. 1 mile per dollar on other purchases. Starting January 24, 2027, the refresh adds 3 miles per dollar on eligible AAdvantage Hotels and AAdvantage Cars bookings, plus 2 miles per dollar in one selected category: U.S. shipping providers, office supply stores or U.S. advertising services. The selected business category can be changed quarterly and has no spending cap. Checked Bags, Boarding And The Companion Certificate The primary cardmember and up to four companions on the same reservation receive a first checked bag free on eligible domestic American Airlines itineraries and Group 5 boarding. You don’t have to buy the ticket with this card to receive those benefits. They follow the primary cardmember’s AAdvantage number on the reservation. An employee traveling separately doesn’t get free checked bags or preferred boarding merely from an employee card. After $30,000 in purchases during a cardmembership year and renewal, the primary cardmember can earn a companion certificate for an eligible domestic Main Cabin roundtrip. The companion pays $99 plus taxes and fees. You buy a qualifying Main Cabin ticket, the companion must have eligible fare inventory available, and you book through American Airlines Meeting Services. Travel is generally within the contiguous 48 states, with additional provisions for residents of Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands. The account must remain open for a full billing cycle after its anniversary month to receive the certificate. The card also offers 10% savings on eligible American Airlines Vacations packages. What The January 24 Refresh Adds To The Citi AAdvantage Business Card The Citi AAdvantage Business Card annual fee rises by $51, and the biggest new credit replaces an existing benefit. Up to $100 in inflight credits each calendar year. Eligible food, beverage and paid Wi-Fi purchases replace the current 25% savings on inflight food and beverages and Wi-Fi. This doesn’t cover purchases in Admirals Clubs. Up to $120 for Global Entry or TSA PreCheck every four years. Useful if you need it, but many readers already have this benefit through another card. 25% off a Melio subscription. This discounts the subscription proposal, not the processing fee charged for paying bills with a credit card. Travel protections. The card adds trip delay, trip cancellation and interruption, lost or damaged luggage, and rental car coverage. Spend $100 on qualifying inflight purchases and the old 25% rebate returned $25. The new credit returns $100, an improvement of $75. After the $51 annual fee increase, you’re $24 ahead on those two changes alone. At $400 in qualifying inflight spending, both versions return $100. Above that, the old uncapped 25% rebate was worth more. I don’t know many people who spent $400 inflight on food and beverages with American Airlines. As I detailed when the changes were confirmed, business card trip delay coverage is up to $500 per covered trip after an eligible delay exceeding six hours, limited to two claims per account in a 12 month period. It isn’t $500 for each traveler. For trip delay and cancellation or interruption coverage, the full covered trip must be paid with the card or an eligible combination of the card and AAdvantage miles, certificates, vouchers, coupons or discounts. When I’d Put Spending On This Card For $100,000 in purchases outside bonus categories, a 2% cash back card would return $2,000. This card produces 100,000 miles. Put that spending on an eligible employee card and it also produces 100,000 Loyalty Points for each of two people. Whether those miles are worth more or less than $2,000 depends on how you use them. The status credit is what can make this a real winning play and it has more value when two people will use the status. If you’re only interested in redeemable miles, other cards can earn more rewards on ordinary spending, including transferable points. Citi’s Strata Premier nad Strata Elite can earn points faster and transfer to American. The business card makes sense for earning status. The Executive Card Can Make This More Valuable The Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive World Legend Mastercard® [See rates and fees] awards 10,000 additional Loyalty Points at each of four thresholds: 50,000, 90,000, 165,000 and 240,000 Loyalty Points in a qualification year. You don’t have to earn the qualifying points by spending on the Executive card. Points from business card spending can trigger the bonuses. Suppose the business primary cardmember and one employee each also hold a separate Executive card as a primary cardmember. Then: $105,000 in eligible purchases on that employee’s business card earns each person 105,000 Loyalty Points. Each person’s Executive card adds 20,000 Loyalty Points from the first two thresholds. Each reaches 125,000 Loyalty Points, enough for Platinum Pro and oneworld Emerald. That requires two separate Executive accounts, each with a $695 annual fee, in addition to the business card. I’ve written about doing this with my wife. I already have the business and Executive cards. Giving her an employee card for the business, and having her hold a separate primary Executive card, could help both of us earn oneworld Emerald from the same business spending. For my family, that has a great use. If we’re flying home from Sydney on an eligible oneworld flight, two Emerald members can each bring a guest into the Qantas first class lounge. We’d have access for all four of us even when we’re flying business class.     In a recent development, the current limited time offer is 75,000 American Airlines AAdvantage bonus miles after $5,000 in purchases within the first five months of account opening. Purchases by the primary cardmember and employees count toward that requirement.

    There’s no annual fee for the first 12 months. The card’s regular annual fee is presently $99, but it rises to $150 with renewals beginning January 24, 2027. Someone opening the card now will see a $150 annual fee at renewal. Employee cards have no additional annual fee, and there’s no foreign transaction fee.

    Industry observers note that the initial bonus alone can cover a one way Japan Airlines business class award between the U.S. and Japan when partner award space is available. American miles remain especially strong for premium cabin awards on partners. Prices largely remain at the same level they were a decade ago, while numerous other progams have devalued.

    Citi’s 48 month restriction applies to an initial bonus on this business card, including its former CitiBusiness AAdvantage Platinum Select-named product. Citi also restricts eligibility after converting another Citi account with a recent initial bonus into this product. Having a separate personal American Airlines card doesn’t, by itself, disqualify you.

    #157164. Hyatt Regency LAX Caps Stays At 21 Days—The Legal Risk That Makes Hotels Turn Away Paying Guests

    📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 27m • 📚 Deep Dive (5313 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Viewfromthewing ↗ Open Full Page

    Hyatt Regency LAX Caps Stays At 21 Days—The Legal Risk That Makes Hotels Turn Away Paying Guests

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 27 min read (5313 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viewfromthewing

    ⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, hyatt Regency LAX won’t let you stay more than 21 consecutive days.
    • Industry observers note that they seem to be worried about a guest becoming a tenant under the law.
    • The hotel does not accept reservations that result in a guest staying more than 21 consecutive days, whether through one reservation or multiple back-to-back reservations.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, hyatt Regency LAX won’t let you stay more than 21 consecutive days. Booking separate reservations won’t get around it. The hotel even counts back-to-back stays. They seem to be worried about a guest becoming a tenant under the law. A customer who wants to keep paying can become someone the hotel needs to turn away. The published policy states: The hotel does not accept reservations that result in a guest staying more than 21 consecutive days, whether through one reservation or multiple back-to-back reservations. Meanwhile, its frequently asked questions advertises “Extended Stay Regency Suites” and tells guests to contact the property about extended stays or special arrangements. Apparently there’s extended, and then there’s too extended. Why A Hotel Might Want You Gone Before A Month I’d put 90% odds at avoiding residential tenancy exposure being the main explanation for this policy. Once someone qualifies as a tenant, ending their stay can require notices and a court eviction instead of ordinary hotel checkout procedures. Depending on the jurisdiction and property, rent regulation and restrictions on the grounds for eviction can enter the picture, too. The hotel may have to spend money establishing that an exception applies before it can get its room back. In the city of Los Angeles, the rent stabilization ordinance brings hotel accommodations occupied as someone’s primary residence for more than 30 days into its definition of a rental unit. Building age and other exemptions matter, too, though. California also has a separate exclusion for qualifying hotels that retain access and control and offer a specified set of services, including housekeeping, mail and room services. The relevant Los Angeles threshold is 30 days. A 21 day limit looks like a conservative buffer, leaving room to deal with a delayed departure before getting close to it. Although a hotel might want to preserve rooms for shorter, more profitable bookings, or limit payment risk. Other Hotels Have Limits, Including Right Next To California In Vegas Hyatt Regency LAX isn’t alone. Here are published limits at some other properties: Hotel Published Stay Limit Hyatt Regency Valencia 28 days Hyatt Regency Westlake 28 days Best Western Los Angeles Worldport, Wilmington 28 days The LINE Los Angeles 29 days, contact the hotel for stays over 21 Wynn Las Vegas / Encore Terms state a 14 day maximum for all reservations Oasis at Gold Spike, Las Vegas 14 consecutive nights The LINE Austin 29 days, contact the hotel for stays over 21 The LINE Washington, D.C. 28 days, contact the hotel for stays over 21 The legal differences at play: Nevada has a 30 day trigger. Its residential landlord-tenant statute excludes hotel or motel occupancy of less than 30 consecutive days, unless the occupant clearly shows an intent to remain for a longer continuous period. Texas looks at the relationship between property and guest. As Texas Legal Aid explains, length of stay, payment arrangements, contract terms, housekeeping and control of the room all help distinguish a guest from a tenant. The state’s 30 day hotel tax exemption also applies. Florida gives the written agreement more weight. Its current definition treats hotel and motel occupancy as transient unless a written rental or lease agreement expressly says the unit is the guest’s sole residence. Transient hotel occupancy is excluded from the residential tenancy chapter. Upcoming York has more than one route to protection. State law includes a nontransient hotel resident in possession for at least 30 consecutive days within its tenant definition for eviction proceedings. But in a New York City hotel covered by rent stabilization, a guest can acquire permanent tenant status much sooner simply by requesting a qualifying lease. Sometimes A Stay Limit Doesn’t Solve The Problem A hotel can’t necessarily make tenancy law disappear by putting a checkout date in its terms. California prohibits a residential hotel from requiring an occupant to move, or check out and re-register, before 30 days when a purpose is keeping them legally transient. That rule applies to residential hotels, not automatically to every hotel. Los Angeles also counts forced room changes and checkouts intended to avoid its rent-stabilization rules. New York City’s rules for covered hotels go further. An occupant who’s never had a lease can request one at any point during occupancy. The request makes them a permanent tenant, and the owner must provide a lease of at least six months within 15 days. The rules also prohibit refusing to continue a tenancy solely to prevent permanent-tenant status. In that setting, a claim can arise after the first night. I understand preventing an apartment landlord from evading the law by calling the building a hotel. But making it difficult for an actual hotel and a willing customer to agree on a temporary stay has costs, too. Someone working on a project, waiting for a home repair, or staying near a hospital may want six weeks of housekeeping and a front desk. They don’t necessarily want an apartment lease. If accommodating that person creates a costly risk of being unable to recover the room, the hotel has an incentive to refuse the booking. The New Yorker Guest Tried To Take The Whole Building The Wyndham New Yorker case I’ve covered took these risks to their absurd extreme. Mickey Barreto booked one night in 2018 for $149 plus tax, requested a lease, and wouldn’t leave. After the hotel removed him, he went to housing court and obtained an order restoring possession of his room. And the hotel subsequently lost a contested eviction case and its appeal. To establish the exemption it claimed from rent stabilization, the property needed to prove that the room rented for more than $350 a month or $88 a week on May 31, 1968. In 2020, an appellate court upheld the eviction case’s dismissal because the hotel hadn’t supplied sufficient evidence. A 1966 hotel directory and a 1969 accountant’s report didn’t establish the necessary room rate on the statutory date. Imagine trying to get your hotel room back in 2020 and losing because you can’t adequately document what it cost in 1968. While the room dispute was going on, Barreto treated his possession order as a basis to claim the entire building. His theory was that the property hadn’t been subdivided, so rights to his room somehow gave him the hotel. He filed documents purporting to transfer ownership to himself and his nonprofit, Mickey Barreto Missions. According to Manhattan prosecutors, he demanded rent from a tenant, demanded control of the hotel’s bank accounts, told the real owner to leave, and approached Wyndham about transferring the franchise. He even went to its lenders to try to borrow against the property. The city recorded fraudulent documents. The courts protected possession of a room. A 2019 judgment declared the deed void and confirmed the real owner’s title. He nevertheless made further false filings in 2023. Tenancy law didn’t authorize stealing a skyscraper. But the hotel was already fighting over a one night guest’s right to remain when it had to start defending its title, its accounts and its dealings with tenants and lenders, too. Barreto was finally evicted in 2024. In February 2026, nearly eight years after checking in, he pleaded guilty to fraud. His sentence was six months already served and five years of probation. Topics on this pageEvictionHyatt Regency LAXLandlord–tenant lawBest Western Hotels & ResortsCaliforniaFloridaLas VegasLos AngelesManhattanNevadaNew YorkTexasWyndham Hotels & Resorts+10 more More From View from the Wing.

The request makes them a permanent tenant, and the owner must provide a lease of at least six months within 15 days. The rules also prohibit refusing to continue a tenancy solely to prevent permanent-tenant status. In that setting, a claim can arise after the first night. I understand preventing an apartment landlord from evading the law by calling the building a hotel. But making it difficult for an actual hotel and a willing customer to agree on a temporary stay has costs, too. Someone working on a project, waiting for a home repair, or staying near a hospital may want six weeks of housekeeping and a front desk. They don’t necessarily want an apartment lease. If accommodating that person creates a costly risk of being unable to recover the room, the hotel has an incentive to refuse the booking. The New Yorker Guest Tried To Take The Whole Building The Wyndham New Yorker case I’ve covered took these risks to their absurd extreme. Mickey Barreto booked one night in 2018 for $149 plus tax, requested a lease, and wouldn’t leave. After the hotel removed him, he went to housing court and obtained an order restoring possession of his room. And the hotel subsequently lost a contested eviction case and its appeal. To establish the exemption it claimed from rent stabilization, the property needed to prove that the room rented for more than $350 a month or $88 a week on May 31, 1968. In 2020, an appellate court upheld the eviction case’s dismissal because the hotel hadn’t supplied sufficient evidence. A 1966 hotel directory and a 1969 accountant’s report didn’t establish the necessary room rate on the statutory date. Imagine trying to get your hotel room back in 2020 and losing because you can’t adequately document what it cost in 1968. While the room dispute was going on, Barreto treated his possession order as a basis to claim the entire building. His theory was that the property hadn’t been subdivided, so rights to his room somehow gave him the hotel. He filed documents purporting to transfer ownership to himself and his nonprofit, Mickey Barreto Missions. According to Manhattan prosecutors, he demanded rent from a tenant, demanded control of the hotel’s bank accounts, told the real owner to leave, and approached Wyndham about transferring the franchise. He even went to its lenders to try to borrow against the property. The city recorded fraudulent documents. The courts protected possession of a room. A 2019 judgment declared the deed void and confirmed the real owner’s title. He nevertheless made further false filings in 2023. Tenancy law didn’t authorize stealing a skyscraper. But the hotel was already fighting over a one night guest’s right to remain when it had to start defending its title, its accounts and its dealings with tenants and lenders, too. Barreto was finally evicted in 2024. In February 2026, nearly eight years after checking in, he pleaded guilty to fraud. His sentence was six months already served and five years of probation.     California also has a separate exclusion for qualifying hotels that retain access and control and offer a specified set of services, including housekeeping, mail and room services.

    BermudAir adds 18 routes, 10 new cities in massive expansion

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that bermudAir is making moves to be a major player in the booming market between the U.S.
    • The airline unveiled a plethora of new routes this past week, marking a major expansion across North American markets, including direct flights to Caribbean destinations.
    • BermudAir will add service from Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport (MSY), Nashville International Airport (BNA), Tweed New Haven Airport (HVN) in Connecticut, Burlington International Airport (BTV) in Vermont, Portland International Jetport (PWM) in Maine, San Antonio International Airport (SAT) and Fredericton International Airport (YFC) in New Brunswick, Canada.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that bermudAir is making moves to be a major player in the booming market between the U.S. and the Caribbean.

    The airline unveiled a plethora of new routes this past week, marking a major expansion across North American markets, including direct flights to Caribbean destinations.

    BermudAir will add service from Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport (MSY), Nashville International Airport (BNA), Tweed New Haven Airport (HVN) in Connecticut, Burlington International Airport (BTV) in Vermont, Portland International Jetport (PWM) in Maine, San Antonio International Airport (SAT) and Fredericton International Airport (YFC) in New Brunswick, Canada.

    Those seven join BermudAir's existing North American airports: Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR), Westchester County Airport (HPN) in Fresh York, Boston Logan International Airport (BOS), Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport (BWI), Raleigh-Durham International Airport (RDU), Orlando Sanford International Airport (SFB), St. Pete–Clearwater International Airport (PIE), Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport (FLL), Toronto Pearson International Airport (YYZ), Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (YUL) and Halifax Stanfield International Airport (YHZ).

    The airline, meanwhile, is adding to its list of direct and nonstop destinations beyond L.F. Wade International Airport (BDA) in Bermuda, with flights to: Ian Fleming International Airport (OCJ) in Ocho Rios, Jamaica; El Salvador International Airport (SAL) in San Salvador, El Salvador; and Ramón Villeda Morales International Airport (SAP) in San Pedro Sula, Honduras.

    The upcoming airports join BermudAir's roster of previously revealed destinations: Clayton J. Lloyd International Airport (AXA) in Anguilla; Philip S.W. Goldson International Airport (BZE) in Belize; Owen Roberts International Airport (GCM) in Grand Cayman; La Aurora International Airport (GUA) in Guatemala; and Providenciales International Airport (PLS) in Turks and Caicos. The airline also offers flights to and from its Bermuda hub.

    Recent findings suggest that "2027 represents an exciting fresh chapter for BermudAir," Adam Scott, BermudAir's founder and CEO, remarked in a statement. "We're bringing our distinctive brand of premium leisure travel to more cities and opening up more opportunities for travelers to experience Bermuda, the Caribbean and Central America.".

    While it is typically difficult for an airline to fly between two countries that are not the airline's home nation, BermudAir notes that it looks to operate the routes as fifth freedom flights originating in Bermuda, Turks and Caicos, Grand Cayman or Anguilla — all British Overseas Territories, which appears to satisfy regulatory statutes.

    BermudAir launched in 2023 as a boutique carrier that planned to run flights between Bermuda and North America using small and efficient Embraer jets. It launched its first flights between North America and other destinations as part of its winter 2026-27 schedule.

    The airline's expansion has been rapid, and if successful, the upcoming routes would make BermudAir a regional force in the Caribbean leisure market.

    What I’m Thankful For

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (244 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Nationalreview

    ⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that I’m thankful for one little moment on Monday this week, around 5:05 p.m.
    • In a recent development, I’m thankful for my older son’s soccer coach, who has known him for over three years now, moving my boy up from an in-house program, to a Sunday league, and this fall to the EDP (Elite Development Program), where this cheap-as-chips town team plays (and usually defeats) all the expensive “academy teams” in our area.
    • Michael Brendan Dougherty is a senior writer at National Review Online.

    Recent findings suggest that I’m thankful for one little moment on Monday this week, around 5:05 p.m. The dark of night was falling over most of the sky, except for a brilliant ring of purple just over the tree line to one side of us. We pulled the minivan into the parking lot of the karate studio, and my eight-year-old son hopped out of the car, grabbing my hand as we passed through the parking lot. I gave it a little squeeze, and he squeezed it back. Maybe just a few more years of that. He earned his first stripes on his white belt that night.

    In a recent development, I’m thankful for my older son’s soccer coach, who has known him for over three years now, moving my boy up from an in-house program, to a Sunday league, and this fall to the EDP (Elite Development Program), where this cheap-as-chips town team plays (and usually defeats) all the expensive “academy teams” in our area. My son was not, at first, a natural athlete — in fact, he was quite clumsy. But he had this enormous engine in him to run, and over the years developed patience for himself to work. His coach recognized him, coached his oversensitivity out of him, made him work — and enjoy working — harder than he ever would have done just by himself.

    Michael Brendan Dougherty is a senior writer at National Review Online.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    On the last day before the 2026 midterm elections, President Donald Trump gave a speech before the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, a site of considerable scandal in his second term. He joked it should be renamed after him and spent considerable time discussing Washington, D.C. construction projects and resurrecting conspiracy theories about monument vandals. When the president did turn to the elections, more than 23 minutes into an hour-long speech, he seemed to foreshadow major Republican losses in the House and Senate, describing it as “The most important midterm, I believe, in our lifetime.”.

    “When you vote, remember a party that hates America cannot be allowed to rule over the people who built our country,” Trump remarked, referring to Democrats, whom he said want to “blow all of this up by electing communist jihadists.”.

    “If the people that voted for me and voted in the last election where we had such a great victory, if they go out and vote, just a good portion of them, we will win in a landslide,” Trump said midway in his speech. “Now that doesn’t happen because usually whoever the sitting president is, Republican or Democrat, uh, good or bad, good president, great president, bad, for some reason the sitting president doesn’t win the midterms, but we gave this a very strong shot.”.

    The last day of polling indicates that Democrats have odds that are better than good to flip control of the House and Senate. The final results from the Upcoming York Times/Siena University polls report “The party is ahead in all seven states likeliest to decide control of the Senate: Michigan, Kansas, Texas, Maine, Ohio and, more narrowly, Alaska and Iowa.” The final predictions in the Cook Political Report included five additional shifts for Democrats in North Carolina, Florida, Tennessee and Virginia, projecting “that Democrats will win 15 to 25 seats, putting them at a 230- to 240-seat majority.” If a sweep happens in the toss up races, it’ll give Democrats their strongest majority since 2009.

    According to recent reports, meanwhile, early voting records have been smashed around the country, in places like South Carolina and Ohio. In Texas, more than 7.7 million voters did so early, surpassing the record turnout for a midterm election set in 2018. Across the nation, about 50 million ballots have already been cast so far, with the share of registered Democrats notably increased in several key state races. But according to the Upcoming York Times, around half the expected votes will come on Election Day itself, making it difficult at this point to determine how substantial a role early votes will play in the outcome.

    #157156. Sacha Baron Cohen reveals “Who Is America?” and the answer is terrifying

    📅 16 Jul 2018 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1886 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Salon ↗ Open Full Page

    Sacha Baron Cohen reveals “Who Is America?” and the answer is terrifying

    📅 16 Jul 2018 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1886 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Salon

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that showtime debuted Sacha Baron Cohen’s latest series on Sunday, finally providing a partial to the question its title poses.
    • Baron Cohen bases his career on that knowledge, but watching it in action was much more entertaining two decades ago in the heyday of “Da Ali G Show.” His HBO prank show became a cultural phenomenon before the omnipresence of social media and its accelerated mainstreaming of conspiracy theory as news, before a sitting president began making the denigration of objective journalism into a sport and before the proliferation of junk science as fact.
    • Sources indicate that back then cameras were not so prevalent as to persuade everyone that they were only one turned corner away from stardom.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that showtime debuted Sacha Baron Cohen’s latest series on Sunday, finally providing a partial to the question its title poses. “Who Is America?” The answer, on its face, will not surprise you: we are a nation of easy marks. Not merely easy, but willing.

    Baron Cohen bases his career on that knowledge, but watching it in action was much more entertaining two decades ago in the heyday of “Da Ali G Show.” His HBO prank show became a cultural phenomenon before the omnipresence of social media and its accelerated mainstreaming of conspiracy theory as news, before a sitting president began making the denigration of objective journalism into a sport and before the proliferation of junk science as fact.

    Sources indicate that back then cameras were not so prevalent as to persuade everyone that they were only one turned corner away from stardom. But today, being on camera is so natural and desirable to most of us that we are willing to say or do just about anything for a few of the 15 minutes we believe to be our birthright.

    “Ali G” and the characters the show introduced, including Borat Sagdiyev and Brüno Gehard, also were born years before Project Veritas and InfoWars and other right-wing vehicles of disinformation made hidden camera hoaxing into something sinister.

    All of which is to say, “Who Is America?” is not, as Showtime would like you to believe, “the most dangerous show in history.” At best, it is an occasionally funny one.

    It has been revealed that but to anyone who mourns the collective deterioration of our population’s capacity to engage in critical thought, but has no idea of how urgent of a crisis that happens to be, Baron Cohen’s upcoming endeavor is less of a comedy than a fright show. “Who Is America?” A nation of pliable dullards ripe for the hacking.

    It has been revealed that “Who Is America?” was produced in secret, and its pre-show marketing largely consisted of publicized declarations of outrage by such right-wing figures as Joe Walsh, Sarah Palin and Roy Moore. Each attempted to transform their extreme embarrassment at having been duped by a British clown hiding behind layers of latex and spirit gum into some approximation of righteous anger at said comedian’s dishonesty.

    It has been revealed that showtime, meanwhile, maintained the aura of mystery surrounding the series almost to the brink of its debut, revealing the title only a little more than a week prior. The network released the briefest of clips featuring one famous interview subject, Dick Cheney.

    This in itself was a bit of flimflam Showtime’s part: “Hope you’ll tune in next week for an interview with me,” Cheney states in the video, only to be a no-show in the premiere.

    In a recent development, you can’t blame “Who Is America?” for saving its biggest fish for later, because the famous politicians in the opener prove the problem of our collective gullibility just fine by themselves. In fact, although liberals may have gotten a hearty guffaw out of hearing Palin’s wailing about having been faked out by Baron Cohen, the very same character — Dr. Billy Wayne Ruddick Jr. PhD of Truthbrary.org — sat down for a conversation with none other than the honorable junior senator from Vermont, Bernie Sanders.

    Prior to the premiere Billy Wayne tweeted a response to Palin’s accusation that he made fun disabled veterans. “I did NOT say I was a War Vet,” Ruddick’s “official” response reads, going on to explain that the service was in was “not military, but United Parcel”.

    Sources indicate that nor does he make such assertions to Sanders, with whom he debates the merits of a universal healthcare plan. And when I say debate, what I mean is that Sanders very calmly shares statistics with Billy Wayne long after the interviewer’s line of questioning stops making sense. And when Sanders asks Billy Wayne to confirm that he is disabled, given that he is conducting the interview while seated on a motorized scooter, Baron Cohen’s character replies that no, he is not. “This here scooter is to preserve my body’s finite energy,” Billy Wayne indicates.

    READ MORE: That viral “strangers on a plane” Twitter story: Not a rom-com but a horror show.

    One may be tempted to qualify Sanders’ appearance by pointing out that he acquitted himself well in the face of a person best be described as a few coconuts short of a beach vacation in Binomo.

    Industry observers note that but this fails to answer the question of why Sanders signed a release, allowing this interview to be broadcast. Did anyone on Sanders’ team vet Truthbrary.org the moment Billy Wayne mentioned it? Even if they thought he was genuine, what is to be gained from being seen in a televised debate with a guy whose site includes a page titled  “Obamanoids — For Real!”?

    In a recent development, (To be fair, reportedly Baron Cohen almost fooled veteran news anchor Ted Koppel as part of his project. Koppel told The Hollywood Reporter that he was contacted to appear in a Showtime project titled “Age of Reason,” said to feature “conversations with distinguished experts in science and public policy, highlighting the brightest and most reputable minds on today’s most vital topics.” Koppel, perhaps receiving brainwaves from his colleague Sam Donaldson, wised up before Baron Cohen could pull him too deeply into his game.).

    A second character introduced in the premiere, an NPR shirt-wearing hyper-liberal named  Nira Cain-N’Degeocello, visits the opulent South Carolina home of wealthy Trump supporters he states are  “afflicted with white privilege.” But it soon becomes clear that his marks’ problem isn’t close-mindedness but over-correcting in the acceptance department. When Baron Cohen’s interviewer waxes on about encouraging his daughter Malala to “free bleed” on the American flag as a lesson, they simply nod and listen; when he chats about his wife’s ongoing affair with a dolphin, they don’t have any questions like, say, whether what they’re hearing is real.

    This brings us to another answer to “Who Is America?”: we’re so aware of cameras, and desperate to have its focus upon us, that we will do and say anything without thinking of its possible permanence.

    Demonstrating this is Baron Cohen’s third character Rick Sherman, an ex-con turned TV host who visits a Laguna Beach, California gallery to show his work, which is a series of capable but otherwise unextraordinary portraits rendered in feces and ejaculate.

    Now, it’s entirely possible that the woman who runs the gallery might have been thinking she could have the next Andres Serrano on her hands. On the other hand, please.

    This is a subject entirely aware of being on view, so obsessed with appearing erudite that while Rick is off camera, having excused himself to the facilities to commit another brown-and-white vision to paper, she addresses the camera like the host she was born to be.

    “Who knew the world was capable of such oxymoronic paradoxical juxtapositions?” she muses. And this is before the homemade pubic hair paintbrush comes out.

    In a recent development, baron Cohen has pushed the limits of tolerant everyday people many times in the past, mostly in a way that makes them look reasonable or, at the very least, more intelligent than the put-ons he inflicts upon them. And this is perhaps one of the most depressing aspects about “Who Is America?”, its demonstration of how endemic our lack of analysis truly is. I’m not saying that gallery owner is a stupid woman, understand.

    It has been revealed that but her interview is an example of prizing exposure over lasting consequence. By that I’m not merely referring to the fact that she placated a man who not only handed her pieces of cardboard purportedly smeared with his own dried excrement, or waited to receive a fresh sample of his work, but that she decided she needed to share her expert observation as to why she needed to do so by uttering a sentence full of five dollar words that add up to absolute nonsense.

    It has been revealed that (Either that or she’s a friend of Baron Cohen’s and in on the gag. I hope it’s option two, as opposed to her actually legitimizing the artistic relevance of number two.).

    A number of reviews of “Who Is America?” have pointed out that Baron Cohen’s sneaky deceit is no longer funny because the formerly insane viewpoints Baron Cohen’s tactics expose have been normalized.

    This has always been the danger, but it’s one every sort of parody or satire contends with in the current climate. It’s difficult to lampoon leaders seeking to legislate ludicrous patches to crises like gun violence instead of adopting common sense solutions like stricter regulation.

    Recent findings suggest that which brings us to the portion of “Who Is America?” guaranteed to dominate Monday’s gallery of crazy clips, fronted by Baron Cohen’s Col. Erran Morad, a self-styled Israeli anti-terrorism expert who calls himself “the terrorist terminator.”.

    The fake Mossad officer is there to promote his “Kinderguardians” program, a proposal that aims to train and arm toddlers in the classroom because, Moran claims, arming teachers is crazy.

    It has been revealed that and this is the portion that has Walsh’s boxers in a bunch, because he joins House representatives Dana Rohrabacher and Joe Wilson in lending on-camera endorsements. Walsh’s comments are interwoven with a series of fake testimonials from the likes of Larry Pratt, executive director emeritus of the lobbying group Gun Owners of America and rape joke enthusiast.

    Nobody forced Walsh to say, with gusto, “The way to stop a bad guy with is a good child with a gun. Happy shooting, kids!” If he didn’t want to say it, he wouldn’t have.

    What Walsh might be upset about is being upstaged by Pratt, who earns some of the episode’s biggest laughs by reading the “science” behind the effectiveness of the fake program, revealing he doesn’t know the difference between human anatomy and hitmakers who grace Billboard’s pop charts.

    In a recent development, yes, “Who Is America?” gets mileage out of highlighting the callousness, sexism and extraordinary gullibility of conservatives, as Baron Cohen always has. But the things they say to him in disguise aren’t all that different than what they’d say on CNN, Fox, MSNBC or talk radio. Whatever power his comedy used to reveal is diminished by the fact that the charlatans no longer operate in secret.

    Next week’s episode introduces one or two upcoming characters, although I don’t imagine they do anything more “dangerous” than the four we met on Sunday. For a number of viewers who love Baron Cohen’s schtick, that won’t matter.

    To them “Who Is America?” is precisely on brand, showing Americans famous and everyday reacting to bizarre situations with varying degrees of what we consider to be normalcy in a time where the baseline version of normal is constantly morphing and shifting.

    Industry observers note that to other viewers, however, “Who Is America?” is a confirmation that Baron Cohen has run some tests and can confirm there is limited and ever decreasing brain activity in this worsening patient we know as America. It is something to behold, that’s for sure. But I’m not sure it’s the stuff of groundbreaking comedy. It’s not even really news.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • President Donald Trump, flanked by Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, gestures during a news conference in the White House briefing room on Friday (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).
    • President Donald Trump stated Friday he might get more accomplished with Democrats running the House and Senate than he did in a Republican-led Congress, but his legislative to-do list differs significantly from the incoming majority party.
    • After previously suggesting he could strike a bipartisan immigration deal with Democrats, Trump on Friday added several items to his wish list after returning Thursday night from a swing across Asia, including several that have support with Democrats with whom he’s bitterly clashed before.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    President Donald Trump, flanked by Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, gestures during a news conference in the White House briefing room on Friday (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    President Donald Trump stated Friday he might get more accomplished with Democrats running the House and Senate than he did in a Republican-led Congress, but his legislative to-do list differs significantly from the incoming majority party.

    After previously suggesting he could strike a bipartisan immigration deal with Democrats, Trump on Friday added several items to his wish list after returning Thursday night from a swing across Asia, including several that have support with Democrats with whom he’s bitterly clashed before.

    Industry observers note that speaking in a stuffy James A. Brady Briefing Room for just shy of 90 minutes, the GOP president contended, without naming a single Democratic leader or lawmaker, that members of the opposition party have called him “about two things in particular,” pointing to health care and immigration.

    “What's happened is I've been called by a lot of Democrats,” he said of the 17 days since Democrats gained dozens of seats across the two chambers. “But people that matter, people that have a lot to do, and they want to talk to me.”.

    But Trump also reminded Democrats that he is more than willing to veto legislation he doesn’t agree with, calling it one of the “extreme powers” of his office and one he might use to bring them to the bargaining table.

    Recent findings suggest that “So they’re going to send things my way, and I’m going to veto them. And then they’re going to send more things, and I’m going to veto them,” he said. “I think, after a month or so, they’re going to send things, and I’m going to say, ’I’m going to veto, unless you want to do this and this and this.”.

    He predicted House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., the likely upcoming speaker of the House, and Sen. Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y., expected to become majority leader, would seek deals because both are “smart.” He would not say if he’d spoken to either leader, but called Jeffries “streetwise,” while noting he had once made a donation to Schumer earlier in their careers.

    Trump went as far as to suggest working across the aisle on health care “may be easier than the Republicans trying to ram it through in reconciliation,” a reference to a fast-track process that allows sprawling bills to pass each chamber with a simple majority — legislation typically needs 60 votes to advance in the Senate.

    The sports-loving president added the Senate-approved “Protect College Sports Act” to his list, and repeated his support for legislation to make Hollywood production companies more competitive. The House moved closer Friday to acting on an amended “Protect” bill when the Rules Committee posted a notice calling for any desired floor amendments by noon on Wednesday.

    “We have to pass that bill,” Trump said. “Every college is going to go bankrupt if we don't get a bill because they're going crazy.”.

    It has been revealed that the Senate’s “Protect” bill would establish the first federal regulatory framework for college athletics, setting national rules for name, image and likeness deals and compensation, as well as installing limitations on agents. It would put in place standards for NIL agreements, create guidelines for schools making direct payments to athletes and provide targeted antitrust protections to certain governing organizations.

    Recent findings suggest that he stated the Senate bill has “tremendous bipartisan support,” but its path in the House remains unclear, according to lobbyists who have worked on the issue. That’s because some House conservatives oppose it and the Congressional Black Caucus has said its members would vote “no.”.

    The CBC has linked it to GOP efforts to redistrict majority minority districts in states the group, with its nearly 60 House members, contends would benefit most from the bill. The CBC is expected to be even larger in the next Congress, further complicating the “Protect” bill’s path to Trump’s desk.

    Recent findings suggest that trump also pointed to the Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act as another possible bipartisan bill. The legislation would establish a federal tax credit to encourage film and television productions to shoot in the United States rather than overseas. Some countries offer American film companies lucrative production incentives to shoot on their soil.

    In a recent development, in a twist, Trump noted Sen. Adam B. Schiff — a longtime foe from the California Democrat’s days probing the president’s alleged ties to Russia as House Intelligence Committee chair during Trump 1.0 — supports that measure.

    In a recent development, “It’s running its way through Congress, and it has unbelievable support. I tell you what, Adam Schiff noted, ‘Wow, we love that bill.’”.

    But the president’s vision of a 120th Congress bipartisan agenda differs from what Democrats have promised.

    Many Democratic incumbents and candidates promised voters they would pursue legislation to lower consumer prices, pare health care costs and end Trump’s Iran conflict, which the president again on Friday acknowledged hurt his party by increasing prices.

    In a recent development, jeffries, during a press conference in Washington on Nov. 4, pointed to reversing the administration’s Medicaid cuts, reviving the Affordable Care Act credits, ending the war and lowering costs as his conference’s “North Star” priorities. This week he also mentioned he would seek to move an immigration-related bill “immediately,” and that the House would “hold the crooks accountable,” a nod to aggressive oversight both chambers are likely to engage in.

    On Iran, reporters pressed Vice President JD Vance over his post-midterms X post blaming the war for the GOP wipeout. One reporter pressed Vance, a potential 2028 Republican presidential hopeful, whether he — like Trump — would start the conflict again. Vance sidestepped as he approached the lectern from behind Trump’s right shoulder, but did not give a full-throated endorsement to go to war again.

    “The president has mentioned he would do it again,” Vance replied. “And my view is that my goal is, and my job is to support the president of the United States.”.

    In a potential 2028 GOP primary preview, Secretary of State Marco Rubio — who has gained ground in some polls since the midterms — was expressionless as he stood a few feet away, positioned behind Trump’s left shoulder.

    Recent findings suggest that trump’s midday press conference marked his first since voters handed Democrats at least 258 House seats and 56 in the Senate come Jan. 3. He again contended the outcome would have been different “if I were on the ballot,” and floated vague conspiracy theories about some falling prices since Democratic candidates bulldozed across the country.

    At one point, he decided to make an announcement that he claimed he had not warned his staff about by floating a threat to U.S. companies that want to build data centers overseas.

    ​"We're going to put a tremendous tax on them, if they do it," he stated, continuing his advocacy of erecting the unpopular facilities across the United States and willingness to use executive powers.

    Sources indicate that as he returned to Washington Thursday night, the White House touted on social media what it called $17 billion in latest deals secured with Asian countries this week. Trump on Friday claimed he told Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. his country would begin buying “100 percent” of its oil from the United States — and Marcos had said, “Yes, sir.”.

    White House aides handed out a one-page “declaration toward peace” before Trump arrived that he later mentioned he had reached with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping.

    The three leaders agreed to ramp up production of petroleum products, pursue unspecified changes to the United Nations and a statement that a “nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought,” according to the White House’s description of the declaration.

    According to recent reports, it also included a line about agreement on the “principle of state consent and respect for immunities of state officials,” an apparent show of support to Putin being targeted by international criminal entities over his conduct of his war with Ukraine. The U.S. president on Friday noted such entities have “fake power.”.

    Industry observers note that trump called the declaration “formal,” as he lauded Chinese cities he was driven through this week as extremely “clean.” He compared them to some Democratic-run U.S. cities and states he described as “so embarrassing” and “dirty.” He dubbed Xi, considered by many Republican and Democratic lawmakers to be a dictator, a “great man.”.

    Some Republican lawmakers who will return for the 120th Congress remarked they have some reservations about Trump meeting with his Chinese and Russian counterparts, doubting Putin’s and Xi’s sincerity about changing course on a number of challenges.

    Retiring Rep. Don Bacon, R-Neb., went further Thursday.

    It has been revealed that “Traditionally, Republicans stood up to Russia and to China. And we stood up for freedom, and we stood up for countries that shared our values,” Bacon, who has floated a potential 2028 presidential bid, said during a National Press Club event. “President Trump has been terrible on this right here.".

    Sources indicate that “He has played footsie with Putin, he’s even blaming Zelenskyy for why the war started,” he added, referring to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. “It infuriates me. And Ronald Reagan is rolling in his grave. … And now the Democrats are talking about the bad Russians and the bad Chinese, and we got to be tougher — it’s another role reversal, here.”.

    • Daniel Foster is a contributing editor at National Review.

    Recent findings suggest that michael Brendan Dougherty has written a piece (“Even Putin Is a ’90s Nostalgist”) that I mostly agree with as far as it goes. My disagreement is largely confined to a few of its asides that nevertheless carry considerable weight for its underlying argument: that NATO expansion in the 1990s and 2000s was a mistake, and that it propelled us toward the unhappy situation NATO finds itself in vis-à-vis an aggressive and acquisitive Russia.

    Industry observers note that I agree of course that Vladimir Putin would like the geographical disposition of NATO as it existed in 1997 but very much not its order of battle. But Michael sees the growth of NATO’s membership as unwieldy and strategically burdensome in light of the reduced military footprint of the alliance. I don’t think that’s right. Rather, the increased size of NATO and its reduced manpower were related and, more importantly, could be seen as strategically offsetting developments.

    Daniel Foster is a contributing editor at National Review.

    On “Strategic Depth for Thee, Not for Me?”.
