    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It’s been a rough year for travel. Oil prices skyrocketed after Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz at the start of the U.S.-Israeli war on the country, leaving many people thinking twice about the steep cost of airfare. More recent disruptions, including to U.S. air traffic control, made us determined to curate a list of holiday gift recommendations that will make you feel globally connected from the comfort of your own home.

    So Brick your phone, set tea to steep with a gooseneck kettle, put on a Mongolian cashmere hoodie, and cozy up to complete a British paint-by-numbers kit while munching on Spanish jamón chips. (Fear not: Those still inclined to travel will also find our favorite bags and gadgets.).

    Recent findings suggest that it’s been a rough year for travel. Oil prices skyrocketed after Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz at the start of the U.S.-Israeli war on the country, leaving many people thinking twice about the steep cost of airfare. More recent disruptions, including to U.S. air traffic control, made us determined to curate a list of holiday gift recommendations that will make you feel globally connected from the comfort of your own home.

    So Brick your phone, set tea to steep with a gooseneck kettle, put on a Mongolian cashmere hoodie, and cozy up to complete a British paint-by-numbers kit while munching on Spanish jamón chips. (Fear not: Those still inclined to travel will also find our favorite bags and gadgets.).

    Baggu Medium Nylon Crescent Bag ($56).

    Recent findings suggest that I’ll be the first to admit that I have a significant problem—er, a bag problem. My closet is practically overflowing with thrifted purses, and my FP colleagues know that I come into the office carrying not one or two sensible totes, but three or four. So trust me when I say that I know bags, and this one stands above the rest.

    Baggu’s Medium Nylon Crescent Bag is a workhorse, ideal for a friend or loved one looking for a trusty companion for weekend errands, jet-setting adventures, and everything in between. I’ve previously recommended Baggu’s packing cubes for their durability and cute patterns. This product has those same qualities.

    Sleek and roomy, the crescent bag is available in a range of colors, materials (mine is leather), and sizes, although I’ve found that the medium-sized pouch is perfect for my needs.

    JisuLife Portable Handheld Fan Ultra2 ($72.67, right now on sale).

    Industry observers note that I’ve traveled to a bunch of countries over the years, but my luggage tag collection is not the largest at FP—not by a long shot. Many of my colleagues have been to more destinations and stayed longer, just one of the things that makes working here so delightful. In the office, everyone has a travel tip.

    In a recent development, mine: The gadgets you take with you should be multifunctional. The exemplar of an all-purpose gadget is this freakishly powerful fan that’s also a power bank, flashlight, and handy-dandy keyboard cleaner. I keep it in my carry-on, fan myself before takeoff, charge my phone over the Atlantic, and light up the seat pocket on arrival to make sure I didn’t leave my passport behind. As for my keyboard—it’s reliably crumb-free.

    Etnodim Ivory Wool Scarf “Zavii” ($122).

    Industry observers note that etnodim makes high-quality, gorgeous interpretations of classical Ukrainian clothes, from embroidered shirts and dresses to traditional kerchiefs. On a trip to Kyiv this fall, I got a traditional shirt, known as a vyshyvanka, for my daughter from their brand store in Podil, Kyiv’s equivalent of Brooklyn. Fortunately, you don’t have to travel 30-plus hours by plane and train to get their items, which are also sold online.

    Recent findings suggest that while I’d heartily recommend Etnodim’s wildly colorful designs, their more basic items—like this merino wool scarf—go with anything. Best of all, you’ll be supporting a Ukrainian brand that celebrates the country’s unique identity, in opposition to Russia’s best efforts to stamp out such cultural expressions.

    Breville Milk Café milk frother ($199.95).

    It has been revealed that after realizing just how much money I was spending per month on lattes at my local (international chain) coffee shop, I decided to look into making them at home. But I didn’t want to spend thousands of dollars on some behemoth machine that requires a specialist degree to operate, either.

    Sources indicate that enter the Breville Milk Café milk frother. It’s super easy to use and clean, it doesn’t take up much counter space, and it reliably makes the perfect steamed milk to my desired temperature and amount of foam. I’ve used it at least once—if not twice—a day for the last five months, and it hasn’t let me down yet.

    Industry observers note that but that’s just the milk part of the equation. Now on to the coffee part….

    Breville Nespresso Original Essenza Mini Espresso Machine ($174.99).

    In a recent development, the Nespresso Original Essenza Mini Espresso Machine is basically a Keurig for espresso. You don’t have to grind beans or fiddle with a million buttons and levers to make a single shot of espresso—just pop in a Nespresso pod; make sure the little, easily removable water tank in the back is full; and hit a button.

    Industry observers note that this machine is also compact, so it doesn’t monopolize your kitchen. Best of all, the espresso tastes just as rich and creamy as it would if you went to the corner coffee shop—and you don’t even have to put on pants to enjoy it.

    —Jennifer Williams, deputy editor.

    Ortlieb Vario Lite pannier backpack ($195).

    FP recently moved offices to a space farther away from the D.C. Metro’s Red Line—and so I became a bike commuter.

    Biking has long been my preferred mode of transportation on the weekends, when I shuttle between yoga and Trader Joe’s with the help of a storage basket. But I quickly realized that commuting is an entirely different ball game. Laptop plus lunch is a heavy—and valuable—combo. I did not trust my basket, however adorable, to keep these items secure.

    In a recent development, enter: a pannier backpack. Rather than settling either for a backpack (which would strain my back while biking and probably make me sweaty) or a pannier (which would be difficult to transport after parking my bike), I decided to invest in this brilliant product from Ortlieb, a German brand that happens to be—like me—Franconian. It has transformed my commute.

    In a recent development, the Vario Lite allows me to toggle seamlessly between pannier and backpack modes. It has an interior laptop pocket and outer compartment where I store my keys and phone for easy access. Its rolltop structure means that its size is flexible, and its backpack function is ergonomic. Did I mention that it’s waterproof, too?

    It has been revealed that the Vario Lite is the little brother of the Vario, a slightly larger pannier backpack from Ortlieb. I tried on both and found the Vario Lite to be a better fit on my 5’1” frame. But anyone can rest assured that there’s an entire line of high-quality pannier backpacks—in a range of colors—to choose from.

    Brick Phone Distraction Blocker ($56.80, currently on sale).

    It has been revealed that the Brick—a magnetic square you can use to curtail access to your phone—is an invention I resisted for a long time. Its very existence was proof that we were living at capitalism’s nadir: You’re telling me I need to buy a little plastic brick to blunt the pernicious effects of this other little plastic brick?

    And yet. The Brick has made my life better, and here are the numbers to back up that claim. Before acquiring the device, I was averaging 10 hours and 40 minutes on my phone per day. Now that number is down to just under eight hours. Sometimes, when there isn’t an international spy scandal all over the news, it has been known to hit seven.

    That I have been wasting this much of my life scrolling is mortifying enough. What’s worse is how easy it was to break the habit. The minor inconvenience the Brick depends on is that once you block certain apps you can only unblock them by tapping your phone to the cube. Tapping the cube is very easy. But most of the time, it’s simply too much of a bother. So instead of doomscrolling, you put down the phone and do something else instead, such as engaging with your children or animals.

    Industry observers note that turns out you can throw money at seemingly intractable problems. Capitalism, you win this round.

    Scotch Precision Ultra Edge Scissors ($11.39).

    I, too, initially recommended the Brick (above) but voluntarily scrapped my write-up lest attention spans wane while reading too many words about a plastic square. Instead, I’d like to recommend something analogue to fill your newfound free time: paper collage.

    I recently turned to physical collaging as a cathartic supplement to the digital work I sometimes do for FP. It’s the perfect hobby for the world traveler with piles of ephemera or magazine readers with a backlog of vintage Foreign Policy and National Geographic. Pull together a gift collage kit with paper bits of your choice and these sharp, precise scissors.

    Sources indicate that these superior snips come recommended secondhand by Ray Orr, a collage artist and former visual journalist and co-founder of Living Room DC, a creative space in D.C.’s Mount Pleasant neighborhood. Consider gifting a workshop or drop-in session for collage or artmaking in the cozy spot.

    —Lori Kelley, executive creative director.

    Cocinare FLOW B9 Gooseneck Electric Kettle ($55.99, at the moment on sale).

    According to recent reports, you know what they say: A warm cup of tea a day keeps the geopolitical crises away. Or maybe two cups, given the present outlook. Actually, scratch that—might be best to have three.

    According to recent reports, world leaders may have decided to shirk responsibility for confronting our warming planet, but you can still control the temperature of water at home with this luxurious electric kettle. No software required; this baby does not run on Outlook. Just plug the kettle in, set it to the optimal steeping temperature for your beverage of choice, and hit the button. A quiet moment with a perfectly warmed cup of tea is just minutes away. (For a slightly less precise but more budget-friendly option, consider this alternative.).

    Everyman’s Library Pocket Classics ($16-$28).

    Recent findings suggest that if you’re like me, packing for a trip is a calculation of how much reading material you can bring to fill time spent in transit without losing precious real estate in your bag. “They’ll have bookstores there,” a wise friend once reminded me. But a smart traveler comes prepared!

    Short story collections from Penguin Random House’s Everyman’s Library Pocket Classics Series are a compact travel companion and a great gift for someone you know who’s getting excited for an upcoming trip (or still reminiscing about their last one).

    It has been revealed that from India to Russia to Ireland, these anthologies compile literary short stories and book excerpts related to the featured country, continent, or city. Their contents can introduce you to a new destination, deepen your appreciation for a place you already love, or even inspire a change of itinerary.

    I’ve found the anthology format to be ideal for the random stretches of time to kill when traveling between destinations. The stories are just the right length to digest on a plane, bus, or train ride, and can even make the inevitable delay more enjoyable.

    Zeedog Ruff Leash ($15.20, right now on sale).

    This year, I became the owner of a young dog—and also the continued owner of pair of aging arms. After having my shoulder wrenched by my puppy’s eagerness to chase D.C.’s rats a few too many times, I switched to this leash from Zeedog.

    Through a simple shock-absorbing design, which looks like a stretchy wave at the end of the leash, the Ruff Leash absorbs the force when your dog yanks. It also comes, like puppies, in a stylish variety of colors. Strongly recommended for anyone foolish enough, like me, to get one.

    Sony WH-1000XM6 Noise-Canceling Headphones ($348, presently on sale).

    Sources indicate that living in a loud city like Latest York, I’ve long been a believer in a good pair of headphones. Even before advances in noise-canceling technology, hearing the Talking Heads instead of the roar of an oncoming subway was an amazing way to mitigate the sounds of crowded urban life.

    Sources indicate that recently, I upgraded from my older Sony headphones to the upcoming WH-1000XM6s. What they lack in catchy brand naming, they make up for in incredible sound quality and call clarity. From Zoom calls to catching background noise in video edits, they sound incredible while blocking out everything I don’t want to hear.

    —Connor Curfman, staff designer.

    Hebe Studio Paint By Numbers Kit ($57).

    I’ve long admired the bold colors and vibrant, travel-inspired scenes painted by Rhi James, the U.K. artist behind Hebe Studio. Her paint-by-numbers kits offer a delightfully nostalgic way to slow down and create beautiful artwork of your own. With these kits—which are designed to be beginner-friendly and include high-quality paints, brushes, and canvas—it’s easy to feel confident as you bring your masterpiece to life. James’s enchanting landscapes are a unique gift that will add a personal touch to someone’s home while also giving them a creative escape.

    —Sara Stewart, senior creative director, product.

    Quince Mongolian Cashmere Pullover Hoodie ($99.90).

    Sources indicate that whether or not you’re comfortable thinking of yourself as the kind of person who wears a cashmere pullover hoodie, you will feel comfortable wearing a cashmere pullover hoodie. Quince cashmere is responsibly and sustainably sourced, so you can also feel comfortable about the conditions of the goat whose soft, soft hair you are wearing. This makes a great gift for anyone whose head gets jealous when they put on a sweater.

    Schoolhouse x Pendleton Abington Hall Throw ($139.99-$238.99, currently on sale).

    As winter approaches, there’s nowhere I want to be but snuggled under a blanket and sitting by a crackling fire. I grew up in the woods of the Pacific Northwest and, to me, Pendleton is the height of luxury. Since 1909, this Oregon-based mill has been producing wool blankets and textiles to outfit lumberjacks and the Beach Boys alike. Pendleton’s collaboration with home goods brand Schoolhouse marries its heritage product with modern style. This 100 percent wool, “Made in USA” blanket is sure to elevate any cozy space and keep you warm all winter long.

    —Rylie Munn, social media editor.

    In a recent development, A confession: I have long known what the perfect holiday gift is, but I’ve kept it to myself. No more! It’s a puzzle from Liberty Puzzles, a wooden jigsaw puzzle made in Boulder, Colorado. (Full disclosure: I worked at Liberty Puzzles long ago, but unlike my friends at fast-food joints, who came away swearing off the menu, I left charmed having seen how the product gets made.).

    Sources indicate that what sets a Liberty Puzzle apart from the typical cardboard variety? For starters, the shapes. Each one is unusual, and thick, laser-cut pieces fall into place with a satisfying click. They also have a faint smell of burnt maple. Best of all, if you ever lose a piece—say, in the stomach of a mischievous furry friend—the company will replace it for free.

    The catalog is quite global, including landscapes, art, maps, and vintage posters, so there’s something for everyone. I’ll make it easy for you: A gastronomical map of Italy for the couple fresh back from their honeymoon! A woodblock print of Japan’s snow-dusted Mount Haruna for the burgeoning snowboarder! A painting of Diana and her nymphs for the Roman history buff in your life! They even make kids’ puzzles.

    Torres Selecta Iberian Ham Gourmet Potato Chips ($49).

    Give the candy canes a break this year and stuff your stockings with chips!

    It has been revealed that I first encountered these pork-flavored potato chips at my neighborhood wine bar years ago, and they quickly became a cult favorite. They’ve been on my mind again, having recently returned from Andalusia, Spain, where jamón ibérico seemed to show up at every meal.

    According to recent reports, salty, savory, and downright decadent, these chips would pair great with a dollop of creme fraiche; a dab of fig jam, pickled shallots, or salmon roe; and a glass of cava. They’re the perfect treat for the adventurous eater on your list, or anyone who’s still dreaming of their last trip.

    —Megan DuBois, associate editor.

    Mens Soft Fleece Drawstring Elastic Waist Cargo Pants ($16.97).

    Yes, you read that right: I’m recommending sweatpants.

    My travel frequency has gone up a lot this year (not a complaint!), and I’ve put a lot of thought into what I wear on long flights. Cargo sweatpants have been a game-changer for comfort and convenience. The additional pockets are useful for carrying chargers, chewing gum, and other paraphernalia without constantly having to open the overhead bin. And the pockets have buttons to close them, so I avoid the constant fear of losing my passport. The sweatpants are also possibly the most comfortable item of clothing I own.

    While I purchased my pair at a brick-and-mortar store in India (shout-out to Marks & Spencer), I’m sure this equivalent on Amazon is just as good. Having closed pockets is the key. And these sweatpants cost less than some Manhattan cocktails, so you can pick up a few to keep in rotation.

    Bic 4-Color Original Retractable Ballpoint Pen ($4.38, right now on sale).

    One of the dangers of having kids is the constant temptation to indulge in nostalgia for the objects of one’s own youth. But sometimes nostalgia can be an invitation to genuine rediscovery.

    It has been revealed that such was my experience with the classic Bic four-color pen. I bought one for my fifth-grade son during this year’s back-to-school run-up and watched as his newfound power dawned. You’re writing in blue, and with a flick of the thumb: Boom! Green. If the mood strikes: Boom! Back to blue—or red?

    I soon bought a four-color pen for myself and promptly came to a renewed appreciation for its simple design and small daily offer of variety. But reading about the pen’s history also gave me a deeper understanding of its geopolitical significance. I hadn’t known that Bic is a French manufacturer, and that the iconic four-color pen has always—since its original release in 1970—been a product proudly made in France. The factory in the town of Montévrain still closely guards its manufacturing secrets.

    The Bic four-color pen isn’t just a writing implement—it’s a precisely engineered machine, an enduring symbol of Francofuturism. All of which makes it the perfect stocking stuffer for the status-conscious middle schooler in your life—or the wonky Europhilic aesthete.

    The Oregon Trail Card Game ($18.50).

    Although I have never been much of a video gamer, I would be lying if I remarked that the 1990s classic Oregon Trail did not eat up hours of my childhood. Fighting to survive bandits, broken axels, and (of course) dysentery was a favorite activity of mine when the days were cold, the nights were long, and I needed an escape from our chaotic world.

    Sources indicate that so when I was gifted a physical version of the iconic game, I was hooked. The story is the same: Make your way from Independence, Missouri, to Willamette Valley, Oregon, without succumbing to drowning, starvation, or a host of other calamities. My friends and I have spent hours around my coffee table attempting to cross the treacherous 2,000-plus-mile passage without incident. There have been screaming matches, thrown cards, and more typhoid outbreaks than we can count.

    And, of course, we have died every time.

    —Alexandra Sharp, World Brief writer.

    Illinois Democratic Gov. JB Pritzker, widely believed to have presidential aspirations in 2028, is facing pushback from conservative education and school choice advocates over a move to opt out of a Trump federal scholarship tax credit program. Critics say the decision was made based on politics and not student outcomes.

    Pritzker revealed Tuesday that the state will opt out of the Trump administration’s Federal Scholarship Tax Credit program, refusing to allow Illinois students to receive scholarships funded through the federal school-choice initiative.

    In a press release, Pritzker argued that participating in what he labeled a "school voucher program" would siphon money and attention away from public education while subsidizing donations to private schools that could discriminate based on religion, sexual orientation or other characteristics.

    GOV KATHY HOCHUL SIGNS NEW YORK ONTO TRUMP'S SCHOOL CHOICE PROGRAM DESPITE TEACHERS UNION OPPOSITION.

    "At a time when public school education needs investments more than ever, we should not siphon money from public schools for private education — especially as the Trump Administration’s policies decimate education," Pritzker wrote.

    Sources indicate that "We have a responsibility to do right by all of our students. Taxpayer funding should not subsidize donations to private schools that could discriminate based on religion, sexual orientation, or other characteristics.".

    According to recent reports, illinois Gov. JB Pritzker holds a news conference in Chicago, Wednesday, June 24, 2026, to sign the Reproductive Health Records Privacy Act (HB 5295) into law. (Terrence Antonio James/Chicago Tribune/Tribune News Service via Getty Images).

    Prominent conservative education activists and groups lambasted the move on social media, making the case that opting in takes nothing away from public schools and that Pritzker’s refusal simply blocks Illinois students from receiving privately funded scholarships while sending Illinois taxpayers’ charitable dollars to students in neighboring states.

    Many also pointed to abysmal test scores in Illinois and noted that Pritzker is siding with the state's powerful teachers unions.

    "It is a remarkably tone-deaf moment from Governor Pritzker, just before Thanksgiving, to deny 1.9 million K-12 students in Illinois access to life-changing educational resources as families are faced with rising costs and an affordability crisis," American Federation for Children CEO Tommy Schultz noted in a press release.

    "Make no mistake: The Education Freedom Tax Credit could have unlocked needed resources for families and students, but Governor Pritzker chose to let those resources go to other states.".

    Schools for America Executive Director Jane McEnaney wrote on X, "Imagine being Governor of Illinois and hating Donald Trump more than you care about the educational opportunities of 1.9 million kids.".

    PROTECTING FAILING SCHOOLS AND SUPPORTING TEACHERS UNIONS IS NOT A WINNABLE STRATEGY, CEO WARNS.

    Students raising hands while teacher asking them questions in classroom. (iStock).

    Pritzker's decision comes after three Democratic governors — Latest York’s Kathy Hochul, Colorado’s Jared Polis and New Mexico’s Michelle Lujan Grisham — agreed to enter the program, saying it brings millions of dollars in additional educational support to students without taking a single cent from public school or state budgets.

    The U. S. Department of Education responded to Pritzker’s press release as well, posting on X that by opting out of the program, Pritzker "just handed scholarship dollars from generous Illinois taxpayers to students in other states instead.".

    Department of Education official Greg Dolan also weighed in on X, saying "the only true thing in this whole statement from @GovPritzker is his name.".

    "May it live in infamy for so callously and cruelly turning his back on helping students in need," Dolan added.

    Erika Sanzi, senior director of communications at Defending Education, told Fox News Digital in an interview that Pritzker’s move was "unconscionable" and a "slap in the face" to parents, who will still be able to write off the taxes. But the money will not go to programs and resources for their children or other students in their state.

    Recent findings suggest that "You don't have to like the program, but can you at least describe it honestly and accurately?" Sanzi remarked about Pritzker’s statement. I am not, but I do think it's disappointing. And I certainly have seen outcry from families in the state that are just extremely frustrated not only by his decision, but by what he mentioned in relation to his decision.".

    Fox News Digital reached out to Pritzker’s office for comment.

    The state's major teachers unions praised Pritzker’s move. Chicago Teachers Union and Illinois Federation of Teachers President Stacy Davis Gates applauded the governor for rejecting what she called "Trump's voucher scheme," arguing that "public dollars belong in public schools" and saying the program would pull money out of public education with "zero oversight.".

    Illinois Education Association President Karl Goeke similarly thanked Pritzker for rejecting vouchers, calling them a "scam" that sends public money to private schools lacking the same testing standards as public schools.

    Don’t Let China Hawks Exploit the Nvidia Scandal

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1261 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Foreignpolicy

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that amid the flurry of commentary over Nvidia and Jensen Huang’s “gone today, here tomorrow” act, there is one question that remains undiscussed: Has U.S.
    • The overwhelming reaction to Huang’s reinstatement has been bipartisan outrage at U.S.
    • Amid the flurry of commentary over Nvidia and Jensen Huang’s “gone today, here tomorrow” act, there is one question that remains undiscussed: Has U.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Get audio access with any FP subscription.

    Recent findings suggest that amid the flurry of commentary over Nvidia and Jensen Huang’s “gone today, here tomorrow” act, there is one question that remains undiscussed: Has U.S. policy toward China succeeded in its aims of maintaining American preeminence and security?

    The overwhelming reaction to Huang’s reinstatement has been bipartisan outrage at U.S. President Donald Trump’s interference in a private company, coupled with demands for stricter enforcement of U.S. export controls on the sale of Nvidia’s chips to China. As Sen. Tom Cotton said, “I have warned the administration from the start about Communist China obtaining our most advanced chips through both smuggling and remote access.”.

    Amid the flurry of commentary over Nvidia and Jensen Huang’s “gone today, here tomorrow” act, there is one question that remains undiscussed: Has U.S. policy toward China succeeded in its aims of maintaining American preeminence and security?

    It has been revealed that the overwhelming reaction to Huang’s reinstatement has been bipartisan outrage at U.S. President Donald Trump’s interference in a private organization, coupled with demands for stricter enforcement of U.S. export controls on the sale of Nvidia’s chips to China. As Sen. Tom Cotton said, “I have warned the administration from the start about Communist China obtaining our most advanced chips through both smuggling and remote access.”.

    According to recent reports, that sentiment is widely shared. But should it be?

    In a recent development, there was a point sometime in the mid-2010s when U.S. policy shifted decisively from engaging China to containing it. This began during U.S. President Barack Obama’s second term, and then it accelerated with the first tariff war and the campaign against Huawei during the first season of the Trump show. It was cemented as consensus policy during the U.S. President Joe Biden’s interregnum and has been maintained during the second season of Trump.

    According to recent reports, this shift was driven by a growing consensus that engagement had failed. China’s entry into the World Trade Organization in 2001 was supposed to make it more democratic and open. It did not. China under President Xi Jinping instead turned away from political reforms, silencing any hint of opposition to the Chinese Communist Party (CCP). Internationally, Beijing adopted a more confrontational stance toward the United States while continuing to steal American intellectual property.

    In this context, Washington embraced export controls on high-end technology that could enhance the Chinese military or give Chinese companies an edge in the race for preeminence in artificial intelligence. But instead of meaningfully containing or slowing China, these export controls have only succeeded in raising tensions and increasing the potential of a future war.

    By most informed accounts, the restrictions in place since 2022 have delayed or impaired the ability of Chinese companies to build AI frontier models on the scale, scope, and speed of Anthropic or OpenAI. The restrictions on semiconductor manufacturing equipment sales to China have also created supply constraints that have pressured the Chinese military.

    As a result, however, China has become far more self-reliant and aggressively built out its own domestic chip design and manufacturing. Though these domestic efforts lag behind the United States, Nvidia, and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Manufacturer by months or even a few years, this has not prevented dramatic breakthroughs such as the unveiling of China’s AI model DeepSeek.

    What’s more, China has managed to evade export controls and obtain high-end chips, either through third parties and other countries in Southeast Asia or through good old-fashioned theft and copying. If Nvidia knowingly and purposely evaded those controls with the acquiescence of some in the Trump administration, that remains a profound scandal. But the reality is that even without this kind of corruption, sanctions have consistently failed to prevent countries from accessing things that are available worldwide, even highly controlled military equipment. A country as large and as intertwined with the global economy as China simply cannot be cut off for long.

    By trying to control China’s chip access and only partly succeeding, Washington has pushed Beijing into a more unequivocally hostile stance. The CCP and Xi perceived, rightly, that the United States had no intention of allowing its peaceful rise and concluded that confrontation was inevitable.

    It has been revealed that especially in the past two years, Washington also began to cut off China’s access to aspects of the domestic U.S. market. The Trump administration has blocked Chinese attempts to purchase U.S. companies and prevented thousands of Chinese students from studying at American universities. Students and investments both made China more dependent on and integrated with the United States.

    According to recent reports, but many Americans, drawing the wrong lessons from the brief period of Japanese ascendency in the late 1980s, saw these developments as a sign of American weakness, not strength. Japan’s investment in Rockefeller Center and Pebble Beach actually bound the country more closely to the United States and in the process demonstrated how attractive and singular U.S. properties and capital markets were (and are). Instead of recognizing this, policymakers simply carried their aversion to foreign investment over to China.

    In a recent development, in the past year, both the Trump administration and Xi seem to have established what was termed “mutually assured disruption.” China can withhold rare-earth exports that are vital to tech companies everywhere, while Washington can use trade restrictions to squeeze the China export machine. The result has been a period of relative calm in U.S.-China tensions.

    Now, with the Nvidia drama, that modus vivendi is in question on Capitol Hill. Congress sees the complicity of the White House as a political opening that it can exploit to double down on its preferred strategy of strangling Chinese technological growth.

    But the calls for greater export controls and more scrutiny of trade will not make the United States economically or militarily more secure. They will instead push China ever deeper into its adversarial stance. In this latest climate, any vestiges of bilateral engagement will be harder to sustain, aggravating the relationship that will determine the stability of the global system over the next decades.

    There is still time to pursue a better policy. From the outset, Washington should have loosened controls on high-end chip exports, which could have helped ease Xi and the CCP’s iron grip on China and soothe bilateral tensions over time. The refrain that the United States can’t afford to let China win the race for artificial general intelligence is grounded in the same fallacy that any country could contain such a technology and that there is some magical first-mover advantage. There certainly wasn’t with any prior technology, nuclear weapons included.

    A more sensible and open policy on chip exports remains the best path going forward. Congress can still pursue it, even as it seeks to hold Trump accountable for any corrupt acts—and Huang for any mistakes he may have made. Nvidia’s scandals do not prove that engagement was wrong and should not preclude the United States and China from developing a more cooperative relationship. Global peace should not be sacrificed on account of Huang’s actions, or Trump’s.

    Zachary Karabell is the author of the Edgy Optimist Substack and an opinion contributor at the Washington Post.

    #157052. La última oportunidad para la paz

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 23m • 📚 Deep Dive (4591 w)

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Foreignaffairs ↗ Open Full Page

    La última oportunidad para la paz

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 23 min read (4591 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Foreignaffairs

    ⏱️ ~23 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • PEDRO SÁNCHEZ es presidente del Gobierno de España.
    • According to recent reports, en algún momento de la última década, el mundo empezó a aceptar la guerra como algo inevitable.
    • In a recent development, no hay nada más peligroso que normalizar la guerra.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    PEDRO SÁNCHEZ es presidente del Gobierno de España.

    Cómo evitar otra guerra mundial.

    According to recent reports, en algún momento de la última década, el mundo empezó a aceptar la guerra como algo inevitable. Las guerras de agresión, como las de Ucrania, el Líbano o Irán, aumentan y siembran horror, ruina y el temor a una confrontación global. Los gobiernos piensan cada vez más en la guerra como algo para lo que hay que prepararse y presupuestar. El gasto militar no deja de crecer, las carreras tecnológicas y armamentísticas se intensifican, y cada vez más países se plantean si deberían dotarse de un arsenal nuclear disuasorio que garantice su seguridad.

    In a recent development, no hay nada más peligroso que normalizar la guerra. Supone regresar a una norma que imperó durante la mayor parte de la historia de la humanidad. La guerra era el eje vertebrador del sistema internacional. Era la vía natural por la que los Estados zanjaban sus disputas o ensanchaban su territorio a costa de vecinos más débiles.

    Industry observers note that pero la inmensa devastación que produjeron las dos guerras mundiales en la primera mitad del siglo XX hizo inaceptable ese statu quo. Los países se unieron en un empeño común: que la guerra dejara de ser un instrumento legítimo de la política de Estado y pasara a ser un acto ilegal. Las guerras no terminaron en 1945, pero durante años la comunidad internacional las condenó de forma abrumadora.

    According to recent reports, en las últimas décadas, sin embargo, el compromiso de los gobiernos con la causa de la paz se ha debilitado. En 2003, millones de personas salieron a las calles en cientos de ciudades para oponerse a la invasión de Irak liderada por Estados Unidos. Y, aun así, la guerra siguió adelante. Iniciada a partir de premisas falsas y en violación del derecho internacional, arrasó Irak, agravó la inestabilidad regional y avivó el resentimiento y el terrorismo contra los países occidentales. Aquel conflicto marcó, además, un punto de inflexión. Desde entonces, la búsqueda de la paz ha ido retrocediendo en la agenda internacional, arrinconada por la creciente competencia geopolítica y la desatención o la indiferencia hacia los esfuerzos multilaterales que durante décadas pusieron freno a la guerra.

    Este camino conduce a una nueva guerra mundial: la catástrofe que el orden del siglo XX se propuso evitar. Ante ese futuro sombrío en el horizonte, los gobiernos deben reaprender el arte de oponerse a la guerra. Todos los países, incluido el mío, España, tienen la responsabilidad de actuar para limitar la capacidad de otros de librar la guerra y para fortalecer las instituciones internacionales que han de ser garantes de la paz.

    Sources indicate that el éxito de este proyecto dependerá de un multilateralismo expansivo, al que yo llamo «maxilateralismo»: una cooperación que abarque al mayor número posible de países, en lugar de limitarse a pequeñas coaliciones ad hoc. Su ambición es que la guerra resulte cada vez más inviable, incluso inimaginable. En 2003, manifestantes por toda España coreaban «¡No a la guerra!». En 2026, el mundo no puede volver a ignorarlos.

    Recent findings suggest that los esfuerzos internacionales por desterrar la guerra como instrumento de política nacional se remontan al Pacto Briand-Kellogg de 1928, un tratado firmado en París por 15 países, al que posteriormente se sumaron decenas más. No bastó para impedir la Segunda Guerra Mundial, pero plantó una semilla. Cuando representantes de 50 países se reunieron en San Francisco en 1945 para crear las Naciones Unidas, recuperaron el espíritu y los principios del Pacto y añadieron lo que había faltado: estructura institucional. La Carta de Naciones Unidas prohibió recurrir a la amenaza o al uso de la fuerza contra la integridad territorial o la independencia política de otro Estado. Y, a diferencia de su predecesor de 1928, respaldó esa prohibición con instituciones facultadas para hacerla cumplir.

    In a recent development, en las décadas siguientes, estas instituciones levantaron un orden que castigaba las violaciones al derecho internacional e incentivaba la cooperación y la diplomacia. Al mismo tiempo, el rechazo popular a la guerra y al militarismo de la Guerra Fría cobraba fuerza en todo el mundo. Se hizo visible en la resistencia a la guerra de Vietnam y en los movimientos de masas contra las armas nucleares. El pacifismo alcanzó su punto álgido en los años noventa, cuando una sociedad civil global pujante se movilizó en defensa de causas humanitarias y Naciones Unidas tenía autoridad para abanderar una ambiciosa agenda de paz.

    Hoy, sin embargo, hay más conflictos armados que en ningún otro momento desde 1946. Según el Programa de Datos sobre Conflictos de Uppsala, en 2025 hubo 65 conflictos activos con participación estatal, el doble que en 2010. Se calcula que en estos conflictos murieron 250.000 personas: la cifra anual más alta desde el genocidio de Ruanda hace más de 30 años. Cerca de 120 millones de personas en todo el mundo siguen desplazadas por la guerra.

    It has been revealed that Y lo más inquietante: las guerras de agresión, que violan la Carta de Naciones Unidas, están de vuelta. Rusia invadió Ucrania. Estados Unidos e Israel atacaron Irán. Y mientras los combates se prolongan año tras año en lugares como el Líbano, Sudán o Yemen, resulta evidente que la guerra está siendo aceptada de nuevo como algo normal.

    Sources indicate that nada indica que esta tendencia vaya a frenarse. Los presupuestos militares se han disparado hasta niveles no vistos en generaciones, en detrimento del gasto social y de desarrollo. Solo en la última década, el gasto mundial en defensa ha aumentado más de un 40 %, y muchos países han duplicado sus presupuestos militares. Los casi 3 billones de dólares que el mundo destina cada año a defensa se acercan al producto interior bruto de todo el continente africano. Incluso países con una larga tradición de contención militar, como Alemania, Dinamarca, Japón y Noruega, se están rearmando a toda velocidad, y algunos están recuperando el servicio militar.

    Sources indicate that aún más estremecedor es el regreso de la amenaza de guerra nuclear. Los nueve Estados con armas nucleares están modernizando sus arsenales y aumentando su capacidad destructiva. Se calcula que el arsenal de China ha pasado de entre unas 200-300 cabezas nucleares a finales de la década de 2010 a 620 este año. Corea del Norte también ha ampliado el suyo, de entre 10-20 cabezas estimadas en 2018 a unas 60 este año, y ha desarrollado plataformas de lanzamiento cada vez más sofisticadas. En marzo, Francia anunció el primer aumento de su número de cabezas nucleares desde 1992. Estados Unidos y Rusia, las dos mayores potencias nucleares del mundo, no han sido capaces de preservar el último tratado que ponía límites a sus arsenales estratégicos. Y cada vez más potencias no nucleares han empezado a plantearse adquirir armas nucleares propias.

    Al mismo tiempo, la inteligencia artificial (IA) está dotando a la guerra de armas cada vez más peligrosas. La supervisión humana se reduce progresivamente a medida que la IA permite automatizar ciberataques contra redes eléctricas, hospitales y sistemas financieros. Hay sistemas de IA que ya han logrado infiltrarse en organismos públicos y han hecho posible la producción masiva de deepfakes y de campañas de desinformación.

    La integración de la IA en las tecnologías nucleares es una amenaza existencial: al acelerar la toma de decisiones, comprime el tiempo disponible para el juicio humano. Del mismo modo, el uso de la IA en biotecnología podría rebajar drásticamente las barreras a la experimentación nociva y al desarrollo de armas biológicas. En ambos terrenos, esta tecnología está elevando a niveles sin precedentes el riesgo de errores de cálculo, de escaladas involuntarias y de destrucción masiva.

    It has been revealed that en conjunto, estas dinámicas multiplican las probabilidades de que cualquier crisis desemboque rápidamente en la aniquilación del planeta. Por desgracia, los países están fabricando los instrumentos de la catástrofe a la velocidad vertiginosa de la innovación, mientras que los instrumentos de control avanzan al ritmo, mucho más lento, de la diplomacia.

    Los cambios políticos están alejando al mundo de la paz. Lo empujan hacia la militarización y la confrontación. Un mundo multipolar no es, por definición, más peligroso. Pero la erosión de las normas y de las instituciones que deberían encauzar las tensiones entre los distintos polos está provocando que el mundo se vuelva especialmente volátil. La competencia entre grandes potencias se intensifica: las ansias de hegemonía alientan políticas exteriores agresivas y los Estados revisionistas desafían las normas y las fronteras establecidas. El nacionalismo beligerante crece. Los movimientos de extrema derecha promueven una visión del mundo en la que las relaciones internacionales son un juego de suma cero y los países deben competir en lugar de cooperar. Incluso dirigentes de centro están adoptando la retórica de la guerra. Aunque no pretendan iniciar una, sus palabras abonan una mentalidad militarista peligrosa.

    En este clima de rivalidad, las guerras de agresión se envuelven en discursos de necesidad, liberación, legítima defensa o justicia histórica. Los agresores presentan sus operaciones como inevitables, después de haber demonizado a sus adversarios para justificar un ataque preventivo. Venden cada guerra como la respuesta a la inseguridad: la guerra que acabará con todas las guerras.

    It has been revealed that pero estas guerras no harán del mundo un lugar más seguro. Cada vez que un Estado desata una guerra de agresión, erosiona las normas que protegen a todos los países frente al uso arbitrario de la fuerza, incluido el propio Estado agresor.

    Las guerras tienen un coste inmenso. Destrozan sociedades y truncan vidas. En 2025, según los registros de Naciones Unidas, al menos un civil murió en conflicto armado cada 14 minutos, y más de cinco millones de personas se vieron obligadas a huir de sus países. El coste económico también es altísimo. La guerra que enfrenta a Estados Unidos e Israel con Irán ha alterado gravemente el comercio marítimo y el tráfico aéreo y ha disparado los precios de la energía, los fertilizantes y otras materias primas. Millones de personas en todo el mundo están sufriendo las consecuencias.

    La guerra genera, además, nuevos peligros. Una vez que empiezan los combates, su rumbo es imprevisible. Los conflictos tienden a arrastrar a nuevos actores y a desbordarse hacia los países vecinos. La guerra de Irán vuelve a ser un ejemplo claro. Desde febrero de 2026, Irán ha atacado objetivos en varios países del Golfo y de su entorno, acciones que España ha condenado sin excepción. Los ataques contra buques civiles y mercantes amenazan la estabilidad del conjunto de la región. Y la guerra ha reavivado los conflictos de Irak, el Líbano y Yemen.

    Industry observers note that por último, las guerras rara vez traen una paz duradera. Al contrario: ahondan los agravios y enquistan las divisiones que alimentan la violencia del mañana. La guerra de Rusia en Ucrania, por ejemplo, ha dinamitado la confianza en Moscú. El genocidio en Gaza ha exacerbado la indignación contra Israel, y eso podría desembocar en nuevas oleadas de terrorismo. Y la guerra contra Irán ha desestabilizado aún más la región y ha lastrado la cooperación entre sus países.

    Recent findings suggest that el mundo tiene la responsabilidad de resistirse a la normalización de la guerra. Callar es un acto de cobardía y de complicidad. La sociedad española está dejando clara su posición: tres de cada cuatro españoles señalan la guerra como su mayor temor. Y un número aún mayor cree que se cierne otra guerra mundial.

    It has been revealed that pero no basta con condenar la guerra en abstracto. La ambición de acabar con ella debe ir acompañada de acciones concretas que hagan cada vez más difícil que los países inicien, sostengan y justifiquen un conflicto armado.

    In a recent development, españa ha procurado actuar en esa dirección. Ha defendido las normas internacionales que marcan la diferencia entre un orden basado en reglas y otro gobernado por la fuerza. Y ha denunciado siempre los ataques armados que violan la Carta de Naciones Unidas.

    Industry observers note that desde el primer día de la guerra en Gaza, España ha reclamado un alto el fuego inmediato y permanente, la liberación de todos los rehenes y la entrada sin restricciones de la ayuda humanitaria. En mayo de 2024, España reconoció el Estado de Palestina con la esperanza de que este paso contribuyera a avanzar hacia una solución negociada y duradera del conflicto. Y ha apoyado activamente los esfuerzos de la Corte Internacional de Justicia y de la Corte Penal Internacional para que los dirigentes israelíes rindan cuentas por sus violaciones del derecho internacional humanitario. Israel tenía derecho a la legítima defensa tras los atentados terroristas del 7 de octubre. Pero ese derecho no justifica el genocidio en Gaza ni la expansión de la ocupación ilegal de Cisjordania.

    Industry observers note that disuadir la guerra exige también elevar el coste de la agresión. El resto del mundo debe asegurarse de que quien elija hacer la guerra no pueda hacerlo sin pagar un precio. A lo largo de la invasión rusa de Ucrania, por ejemplo, la Unión Europea ha aprobado sucesivas rondas de sanciones contra Rusia que España ha respaldado sin titubeos. España también ha prestado a Ucrania ayuda financiera, humanitaria y militar para que pueda defender su territorio y negarle a Rusia el botín de guerra.

    It has been revealed that los países deben negarse a ayudar a las partes a extender los conflictos en curso. España, por ejemplo, mantiene un embargo de armas a Israel desde 2023. Este año, además, negó a Estados Unidos el uso de su territorio y de sus instalaciones para la guerra contra Irán. La decisión de España no fue un acto de hostilidad hacia un aliado. Tampoco fue una expresión de neutralidad ni de simpatía hacia el régimen iraní. Fue el fruto de una valoración estratégica: implicarse habría favorecido la escalada del conflicto y agravado la inseguridad regional y mundial. Para ser fiel a su compromiso con la paz, España tenía que estar dispuesta a decir no, aunque eso tuviera un coste político. Si más países hubieran actuado igual, las guerras de Gaza y de Irán habrían sido mucho más difíciles y costosas de librar.

    Invertir en prosperidad es igualmente esencial. La seguridad crece cuando las sociedades son resilientes, las desigualdades se reducen y la ciudadanía puede confiar en las instituciones públicas. La decisión de España, el año pasado, de no asumir el objetivo de gasto en defensa del 5 % del PIB propuesto por la OTAN refleja esta visión. No nace de una falta de compromiso con la defensa europea. De hecho, mi Gobierno ha sido uno de los principales impulsores de la autonomía estratégica de la Unión Europea, triplicando el gasto neto en defensa en los ocho años que llevo en el cargo. Pero la disuasión militar y el bienestar social deben reforzarse mutuamente. Al mantener un gasto en defensa proporcionado, España ha conservado el margen fiscal necesario para invertir 145.000 millones de euros adicionales en protección social, vivienda, sanidad y educación, y más de 30.000 millones en la transición ecológica. Son políticas que cohesionan la sociedad y, por tanto, la hacen más segura.

    Sources indicate that los esfuerzos de un solo país tienen, sin embargo, un alcance limitado. Cortarle el oxígeno a la guerra exige la implicación de todos: un esfuerzo colectivo basado en un multilateralismo genuino. Esta es la única estrategia que ha funcionado en el pasado. El sistema multilateral construido tras la Segunda Guerra Mundial abarcaba todo el planeta y contribuyó a preservar la paz entre las grandes potencias y a evitar una tercera guerra mundial.

    Reforzarlo no será tarea fácil. La pugna geopolítica y una desconfianza generalizada han debilitado a Naciones Unidas, los organismos financieros internacionales, las organizaciones regionales y otras instituciones multilaterales. Muchos países las perciben como ineficaces y atrapadas en una crisis perpetua, de modo que están recurriendo a marcos alternativos para intentar poner fin a las guerras.

    Recent findings suggest that algunos han optado por enfoques unilaterales, persiguiendo acuerdos transaccionales que acaban beneficiando a élites económicas y políticas y dejan al margen a las poblaciones afectadas por el conflicto. Los altos el fuego o los acuerdos de paz que logran pueden ser preferibles a la continuación de la guerra, pero cualquier paz impuesta por la ley del más fuerte, y no por el derecho, se asienta sobre cimientos frágiles.

    In a recent development, otros países, frustrados con el multilateralismo, han intentado formar «coaliciones de voluntarios» u otros grupos «minilaterales» para garantizar su seguridad o alcanzar acuerdos ad hoc en materia de comercio o tecnología. Este enfoque puede ser una solución temporal a la parálisis de las instituciones tradicionales, pero su carácter excluyente fragmenta aún más un orden internacional ya dividido. Lo que necesitamos no es minilateralismo, sino maxilateralismo. La cooperación internacional alcanza su verdadera fuerza cuando es—o aspira a ser—universal. Dejar a una parte del mundo fuera de estos esfuerzos es, además, incubar la confrontación de mañana.

    In a recent development, el sistema internacional del siglo XX no era perfecto. Sus normas se han aplicado de manera desigual, sus principios se han defendido de forma inconsistente y sus procedimientos han sido desesperantemente lentos. Pero es innegable que, sin él, el mundo sería un polvorín aún mayor. Basta un ejemplo: fue una red de tratados internacionales—entre ellos, el Tratado sobre la No Proliferación de las Armas Nucleares, el Tratado sobre Fuerzas Nucleares de Alcance Intermedio y el Tratado de Prohibición Parcial de los Ensayos Nucleares—la que puso fin a una carrera armamentística desbocada y extraordinariamente costosa que estaba llevando al mundo al borde de una guerra nuclear.

    Sources indicate that toda esta arquitectura institucional se está resquebrajando. Y sin ella, aspirar a preservar la paz es una quimera.

    Recent findings suggest that fortalecer las instituciones multilaterales debe ser el eje central de una campaña global para relegar la guerra a los libros de historia. Para ello será necesario acometer reformas de calado que les devuelvan la legitimidad y refuercen su capacidad de actuación, dando prioridad a las medidas que más contribuyan a la paz y la seguridad.

    According to recent reports, la primera pasa por aumentar la representación en las Naciones Unidas y las instituciones de Bretton Woods. Actualizar la estructura del Consejo de Seguridad de Naciones Unidas es especialmente importante, dada su responsabilidad principal de mantener la paz internacional. Un Consejo de Seguridad con asientos permanentes y derecho de veto para las cinco potencias vencedoras de la Segunda Guerra Mundial, que en conjunto suman apenas una cuarta parte de la población mundial, no refleja el mundo de hoy. Debe ampliarse el número de miembros electos del Consejo y alargar su mandato más allá de los dos años actuales. Los nuevos asientos deben otorgarse principalmente a países de regiones infrarrepresentadas, en particular África y América Latina. Organizaciones regionales como la Unión Europea y la Unión Africana también deberían estar representadas en el Consejo, posiblemente ocupando puestos que hoy corresponden a Estados. Un Consejo de Seguridad más representativo no solo sería más justo, sino también más eficaz. Los países defienden y hacen cumplir con más empeño las normas internacionales cuando se sienten autores de ellas.

    Industry observers note that también hay que restringir estrictamente el poder de veto de los miembros permanentes, en especial cuando el Consejo de Seguridad delibere sobre casos de atrocidades masivas, genocidio, crímenes de lesa humanidad y crímenes de guerra. En última instancia, el veto debe abolirse por completo. Solo entonces podrá el Consejo responder a todos los actos de agresión sin quedar secuestrado por las objeciones de un solo Estado.

    Industry observers note that un espíritu similar debería orientar la transformación estructural de las instituciones financieras internacionales, en particular el Fondo Monetario Internacional y el Banco Mundial. La distribución del poder de voto en ambas sigue reflejando los equilibrios económicos del siglo XX y, por convención, un europeo está siempre al frente del FMI y un estadounidense, del Banco Mundial. Esto debe terminar. Las economías emergentes necesitan una representación más adecuada, y los puestos de liderazgo deben estar abiertos a todos los candidatos, sea cual sea su nacionalidad. También deberán evolucionar las responsabilidades que asumen en instituciones como la Organización Mundial del Comercio los países antes considerados «en desarrollo», a medida que crecen y se incorporan al grupo de las economías más ricas. Una gobernanza económica más justa aliviaría la desigualdad y el resentimiento que con tanta frecuencia atizan la inestabilidad y los conflictos.

    Otra reforma esencial consiste en revitalizar el marco internacional que contiene el riesgo de escalada nuclear. Parte de ese trabajo depende de las potencias nucleares. Corresponde a Estados Unidos y a Rusia negociar un tratado que suceda al acuerdo bilateral Nuevo START y que preserve topes verificables al despliegue de armas nucleares. Y, esta vez, China debería participar en las conversaciones.

    Pero el esfuerzo más amplio exige el compromiso de todos los países. Entre sus prioridades deben figurar la ratificación del Tratado de Prohibición Completa de los Ensayos Nucleares, para impedir que se reanuden las pruebas nucleares, y el avance de las negociaciones sobre un Tratado de Prohibición de la Producción de Material Fisionable, que prohibiría la producción de uranio altamente enriquecido y plutonio para armas nucleares. Todos deben también trabajar conjuntamente para regular el uso de la IA en el ámbito militar, especialmente en lo que respecta a las armas nucleares, a fin de preservar el control humano sobre las decisiones de lanzamiento y minimizar el riesgo de errores fatales. Los países no nucleares deben comprometerse a no adquirir armas nucleares y deben emplear todos los medios a su alcance para instar a las potencias nucleares a reducir sus arsenales, reforzar los mecanismos de verificación y reconstruir las salvaguardas diplomáticas que durante décadas han ayudado a evitar una catástrofe nuclear.

    According to recent reports, la tecnología puede contribuir en parte a esta tarea. Los avances en imágenes por satélite, sensores remotos y análisis de datos pueden aumentar la transparencia y la supervisión del cumplimiento de los acuerdos de control de armamentos. Pero también hay que hacer mucho más para evitar situaciones que puedan precipitar una guerra. Si los Estados con armas nucleares acuerdan reducir su disponibilidad operacional y reforzar la comunicación en momentos de tensión, los gobiernos contarán con más tiempo y más medios para desactivar las crisis. Cada país debe proteger sus sistemas de mando y control frente a los ciberataques y la manipulación informativa impulsada por la IA, de modo que una falsa alarma o un error de cálculo no desencadenen jamás una guerra nuclear.

    Por último, es prioritario trabajar para garantizar que el sistema de justicia internacional pueda hacer cumplir las decisiones de los tribunales. Desmantelar la Corte Penal Internacional, como pretenden algunos países, solo aseguraría la impunidad de los crímenes más atroces. La CPI no solo debe investigar y juzgar los casos de genocidio, agresión, crímenes de guerra y crímenes de lesa humanidad, sino también contar con la autoridad necesaria para llevar ante la justicia a los responsables de esos crímenes. Cuando un Estado pasa a ser parte del Estatuto de Roma, el tratado que creó la CPI, acepta someterse a la jurisdicción de la Corte. Sin embargo, si ese Estado se niega a cooperar o a entregar a un sospechoso, no existe una sanción efectiva, sino apenas una llamada de atención. Esto debe cambiar. Los Estados que den cobijo a personas imputadas por la CPI deben afrontar consecuencias legales, diplomáticas y financieras. Iniciar y librar una guerra debe tener un coste real.

    La reforma de las instituciones internacionales lleva años estancada, pero la próxima elección para la Secretaría General de Naciones Unidas ofrece una ocasión excepcional para darle un nuevo impulso. Que Naciones Unidas nombrara a su primera secretaria general sería un poderoso símbolo de renovación, inclusión y adaptación institucional. La organización no puede afirmar verdaderamente que habla en nombre de toda la humanidad mientras no la haya dirigido una mujer. Alcanzar este hito podría despertar una nueva ambición y reforzar la confianza en la capacidad de las instituciones internacionales para reformarse y para que recuperen su papel a la hora de poner freno a la guerra.

    Frenar la deriva del mundo hacia la guerra exigirá el compromiso más amplio posible. Ningún país, grande o pequeño, puede mirar hacia otro lado ni sumarse a las acciones que aviven la escalada. Todos debemos defender las normas internacionales que hoy ponen coto a la guerra y reformar y dotar de poder a las instituciones que mañana la harán imposible.

    Industry observers note that en última instancia, lo que hará inimaginable la guerra es una agenda de paz positiva que aborde las causas profundas de la inseguridad. Cada paso hacia la erradicación de la pobreza, la ampliación del acceso a una educación de calidad, el avance de la igualdad de género, el fortalecimiento de las instituciones democráticas y el aumento de la resiliencia ante los desastres naturales atenúa también las condiciones que engendran la violencia.

    Las instituciones financieras internacionales deben ser capaces de proporcionar financiación con rapidez, a gran escala y a un coste razonable, para que ningún país en desarrollo se vea obligado a elegir entre atender su deuda e invertir en su población. Los bancos multilaterales de desarrollo deben poder movilizar fondos para las transiciones ecológica y digital, de modo que las migraciones climáticas y la disputa por los recursos no se conviertan en detonantes de conflictos entre Estados. Y el Acuerdo sobre Pandemias de la Organización Mundial de la Salud debe ultimarse y entrar en vigor para garantizar que todos los países puedan acceder a vacunas y tratamientos cuando llegue la próxima emergencia sanitaria mundial.

    Industry observers note that por eso España ha procurado situar el desarrollo en el centro de su política exterior. El Gobierno español ha sido un firme defensor de los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible de la ONU para 2030 y, el año pasado, la ciudad de Sevilla acogió la Cuarta Conferencia Internacional sobre la Financiación para el Desarrollo, donde la comunidad internacional se comprometió a aligerar la carga de la deuda de los países vulnerables y a desbloquear inversiones para el desarrollo sostenible. España también ha promovido iniciativas como el Centro Global para Canjes de Deuda por Desarrollo, lanzado junto con el Banco Mundial; la Alianza multilateral por las Cláusulas de Suspensión de Deuda, que permite a los países vulnerables suspender el pago de su deuda tras una catástrofe; y un mecanismo propio para ofrecer hasta 60 millones de euros anuales en alivio de deuda a países en desarrollo. Además, España ha respaldado, junto con instituciones multilaterales y organizaciones internacionales, iniciativas de financiación climática, salud global, igualdad de género, seguridad alimentaria y protección social. Estas políticas de desarrollo son también políticas de construcción de paz.

    It has been revealed that un proyecto ambicioso de movilización global en favor del derecho internacional y de un multilateralismo genuino puede parecer poco realista. Pero ya hemos visto lo que ocurre cuando la normalización de la guerra arrastra a la humanidad al infierno. Los hombres y las mujeres que se levantaron de entre las ruinas de la Segunda Guerra Mundial, el capítulo más oscuro de nuestra historia, encontraron la manera de construir un orden mundial multilateral. La pregunta a la que se enfrenta nuestra generación es si seremos capaces de preservar el imperio de la ley o permitiremos el regreso de la ley de la jungla. Si construiremos el mundo del mañana con visión de futuro y cooperación, o a través del caos y del dolor de otra guerra mundial. Debemos elegir bien mientras la decisión siga estando en nuestras manos.

    Sen. Ruben Gallego, D-Ariz., says he's willing to work with Rep. Maria Elvira Salazar, R-Fla., to pass her immigration reform agenda in the U.S. Senate.

    House Republicans are optimistic that President Donald Trump could sign a bipartisan immigration reform bill before Democrats take control of Congress.

    They warn that if the president waits until January it could result in legislation containing more "extreme" language that opens the door for amnesty.

    "Yes, it's going to happen under this Congress," Rep. Don Bacon, R-Neb., told Fox News Digital, pointing to the country's labor shortages and Republicans' declining support among Hispanic voters as reasons to pursue immigration reform. "I think it's a win-win for a country, we get a much-needed workforce while providing some accountability for misbehavior.".

    Bacon's remarks come after Trump signaled during a recent "60 Minutes" interview that he would be open to immigration reform, potentially creating an opportunity for lawmakers to advance the Dignity Act, a bill introduced by Rep. Maria Elvira Salazar, R-Fla., in 2025.

    WHITE HOUSE DOUBLES DOWN AFTER TRUMP ANGERS BASE BY FLOATING ILLEGAL ALIEN DEAL WITH DEMS.

    The legislation, which now has over a dozen Republican co-sponsors, would provide certain undocumented immigrants who meet eligibility requirements with renewable legal status and work authorization, without establishing a direct pathway to citizenship.

    However, Bacon warned that delaying the legislation until the 120th Congress, when Democrats will control both chambers, could result in a more expansive immigration package.

    Recent findings suggest that "Unfortunately, I think the Dems will make it more like an amnesty bill," Bacon told Fox News Digital. "They'll probably go to another extreme.".

    Rep. Marlin Stutzman, R-Ind., added to Fox News Digital that "there is no better solution on the table that will get support from both parties while simultaneously standing in the way of the Democrats' looming amnesty-ridden citizenship-for-all alternative.".

    "The best way to see the work the administration is doing continue into the next two years while Democrats are in control of both houses is to pass a Republican-led immigration plan before January," Stutzman continued.

    GOP INFIGHTING ERUPTS OVER IMMIGRATION BILL THAT WOULD SHIELD MILLIONS FROM DEPORTATION.

    Rep. Maria Elvira Salazar, R-Fla., arrives for the House Republican Conference caucus meeting in the U.S. Capitol on Tuesday, Sept. 1, 2026. (Bill Clark/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images).

    Salazar previously told Fox News Digital that Trump's willingness to discuss immigration reform could create an opportunity to advance her legislation before Republicans lose control of Congress.

    "I think that this is a very good window to concentrate on something that even the president said that he was willing to work with the Dems, which is immigration," Salazar said.

    TRUMP ADMITS IMMIGRATION ENFORCEMENT MAY HAVE BEEN TOO 'TOUGH' IN FIRST INTERVIEW SINCE MIDTERMS.

    The bill's original sponsor also expressed hope that Trump could make immigration reform a defining part of his presidential legacy, comparing the opportunity to Abraham Lincoln's role in ending slavery.

    • President Donald Trump, first lady Melania Trump and Speaker Mike Johnson are all smiles at the annual Thanksgiving turkey pardon at the White House.

    • Joined by first lady Melania Trump and Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., set to lose power in January after he hands the gavel to a Democratic successor, Trump for the sixth time spared the long necks of two American turkeys — this time “Feathers” and “Freedom.”.

    President Donald Trump, first lady Melania Trump and Speaker Mike Johnson are all smiles at the annual Thanksgiving turkey pardon at the White House. (Finn Gomez/Getty Images).

    President Donald Trump on Tuesday celebrated what he called one of the “immense powers” of his office, pardoning two turkeys ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday. But lawmakers say his influence on Capitol Hill has already changed since Republicans’ midterm losses.

    Joined by first lady Melania Trump and Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., set to lose power in January after he hands the gavel to a Democratic successor, Trump for the sixth time spared the long necks of two American turkeys — this time “Feathers” and “Freedom.”.

    “In a few moments, under the immense powers vested in me by the Constitution of the United States of America, I will grant a full, absolute and unconditional pardon — meaning they will live forever — to two magnificent Thanksgiving turkeys, special turkeys,” Trump noted, suggesting he could extend his power to spare the birds from the holiday dining table to somehow grant them immortality.

    While voters punished his party’s candidates for doing too little to address high prices and his decision to join Israel in going to war with Iran, Trump on Tuesday remained focused on another area of largely unchallenged authority — his White House projects. He began the event by touting the yearly event, for the first time, being held on the helipad he had built on the White House’s South Lawn. Later, he announced looks for another new location next year.

    “I'm told that per the long-running tradition, these exquisite animals stayed overnight at the nearby Willard Hotel. Unfortunately, for 200 years, the White House lacked appropriate accommodation to host such distinguished guests,” he remarked of the turkeys. “I'm pleased to announce that next year we'll be able to have a special location right over there in that rather small ballroom being built. It's going to host a lot of people and a couple of turkeys next year. We're going to do it inside.”.

    Sources indicate that trump also highlighted that the two bright, white turkeys were raised in West Virginia — which he carried more than 40 points when he was on the ballot. The turkeys, now spared, will spend their remaining years in Texas, a state where Democrats scored two of their most high profile wins in the House and Senate races — something Trump left unmentioned.

    Sources indicate that the pre-holiday vibes were lighthearted on Tuesday, with the president slated to later travel to South Florida for a Thanksgiving weekend of turkey and time at one of his golf clubs. But when he returns, lawmakers will continue assessing how much sway he still has on Capitol Hill as he begins what, for his predecessors, were their lame-duck eras.

    One Republican Senate ally acknowledged his influence with lawmakers already has changed.

    “I think it's going to be policy-to-policy on that,” mentioned Senate Republican Conference Vice Chair James Lankford.

    According to recent reports, “But he's the president of the United States all the way to the very end. So he still has his veto pen,” the Oklahoman added. “He still has the ability to be able to direct agencies to engage. We're passing legislation. It takes three to tango: House, Senate, and the White House.”.

    Recent findings suggest that senate Commerce Committee Chair Ted Cruz of Texas remarked Trump’s influence, once the Democrat-controlled House and Senate are seated on Jan. 3, “will, obviously, be different.”.

    “I don't think the incoming Democrat majorities are interested in passing productive legislation and passing pro-jobs legislation,” said Cruz, a potential 2028 GOP presidential candidate. “I think, instead, they're just going to attack the president all day long.”.

    Still, Cruz predicted “the president will continue to lead.”.

    Trump on Monday showed how he likely intends to use his lame-duck influence on and off Capitol Hill when he successfully pushed for the reinstatement of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. During an interview with CNBC’s Eamon Javers, Trump made an admission that would be stunning from any other sitting American president about a private company, saying he had been “speaking to the board directly and indirectly.”.

    In a Monday statement, Nvidia said its board had “received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.”.

    Recent findings suggest that such unprecedented moves are a massive reason why Sen. Rick Scott, R-Fla., last week mentioned he expects Trump to be Trump — despite overseeing a midterms campaign he insisted be about himself and his unpopular second-term record.

    According to recent reports, “Any president is going to have a lot of influence because they get to run the executive branch,” said Scott, a former Sunshine State chief executive. “And they have the biggest pulpit in the world. So he's going to continue to have a lot of influence.”.

    Still, some Republican lawmakers have criticized Trump and his team for what they call recent stumbles.

    Sen. Jim Banks of Indiana last week told reporters he had “a lot of questions” about how Trump and his administration handled upgrades to the country’s air traffic control system that prompted a nationwide ground stop on Nov. 13.

    “Somebody needs to be held accountable for what happened,” he mentioned, raising concerns about the president demanding $50 billion in additional taxpayer monies to build a new system. “I’m not fully convinced that throwing out more money is going to solve the fundamental problems.”.

    Trump also has taken ample friendly fire on social media from GOP members over his interference in the Huang scandal.

    According to recent reports, north Carolina GOP Rep. Pat Harrigan took to X to say the Nvidia founder’s reinstatement was “a mistake.”.

    “For the past two years, I have privately said there is no way Jensen Huang can argue for the exportation of advanced American chips to China without being compromised. Turns out, well, we all know,” Harrigan wrote after Trump contended an administration probe had “exonerated” Huang of any potential wrongdoing. “There may come a time when forgiveness is warranted, but there are still too many unanswered questions and too much unmitigated risk. Today’s coordinated action between the company and this administration is likely to whitewash this risk.”.

    Harrigan, a rare Tar Heel State Republican incumbent to win another term, echoed other GOP lawmakers in calling for an in-depth congressional probe in the Huang scandal and his affair with an alleged Chinese intelligence operative.

    Next week could offer an early test of other Republicans’ willingness to break more publicly with Trump on certain issues, as Huang is scheduled to appear before multiple congressional committees.

    Sources indicate that even before Trump threw his political weight behind Huang’s return, Democratic Sen. Tim Kaine of Virginia said he had sensed a GOP president who had lost clout with his party’s Senate conference.

    “I think the Nvidia matter has caused some major concerns about the Trump China policy, obviously,” Kaine said. “That is definitely creating some anxiety.”.

    Trump has given clues that he is as concerned with his influence among the incoming Democratic majorities.

    Sources indicate that “If they want to get things done, I want to get things done, too,” Trump said during a Friday press conference at the White House. “You know, there are those that say we might get more done because we had some Republicans that were just impossible to deal with.”.
